ruvnet/ruflo.what: Ruflo (formerly Claude Flow) is an add-on layer for Claude Code and Codex that installs many predefined agents, slash commands, hooks, a memory database and an MCP server so that several AI agents can work on a task as a coordinated 'swarm'.
ruvnet/ruflo.why: It aims to turn a single coding assistant into a team of specialised agents that plan, remember past sessions and hand work to each other. People reach for it when they want multi-agent orchestration inside Claude Code without building it themselves.
ruvnet/ruflo.start: npx ruflo init (or, lighter: /plugin marketplace add ruvnet/ruflo in Claude Code)
ruvnet/ruflo.caution: Very large surface area: the README itself mentions 314 MCP tools, 35 plugins and ~100 agents, and the full install writes .claude/, .claude-flow/, CLAUDE.md, hooks and a background daemon into your project. Claims about 'self-learning' and 'swarm intelligence' are the project's own; start with a single plugin before the full install, and expect more token use when many agents run.
ruvnet/ruflo.plain: An add-on that lets Claude Code run a team of AI helpers that split up and share a task.
useFor: Split a large coding project across several AI helpers
Keep notes from past sessions so the AI remembers context
Add ready-made agents and commands to Claude Code
steps: Install Claude Code first, since Ruflo is an add-on for it.
For a light start, inside Claude Code type `/plugin marketplace add ruvnet/ruflo`.
Install one plugin first; the full install writes many files and a background service into your project.
Watch your usage, because several agents running together use more tokens.

diegosouzapw/OmniRoute.what: OmniRoute is a self-hosted gateway that gives coding tools one local OpenAI-compatible address (localhost:20128) and forwards requests to hundreds of AI providers, with a focus on combining free tiers and falling back automatically when one runs out.
diegosouzapw/OmniRoute.why: It is for people who want to keep Claude Code, Cursor, Cline or Codex running on free or cheap model quotas without juggling many API keys and rate limits by hand. It also adds prompt compression, a dashboard and quota tracking.
diegosouzapw/OmniRoute.start: npm install -g omniroute, then point your tool at http://localhost:20128/v1
diegosouzapw/OmniRoute.caution: The headline figures (350+ providers, ~1.6B free tokens/month, 15-95% token savings) are the project's own claims, and the README notes the free-tier numbers change as providers change their terms. Routing your code through many third-party free providers has privacy implications, and some providers' terms may not allow this kind of pooling; check what each provider does with your data.
diegosouzapw/OmniRoute.plain: A program on your computer that sends your AI tool's requests to whichever free AI service still has room.
useFor: Keep Claude Code or Cursor running on free model quotas
Switch to another provider automatically when one runs out
Track how much of each free quota you have used
steps: Install Node.js, which includes the npm installer.
In a terminal, run `npm install -g omniroute`.
In your coding tool's settings, set the server address to localhost port 20128, as the README explains.
Check what each provider does with your code before sending it through them.

BerriAI/litellm.what: LiteLLM is a Python library and a self-hosted proxy server that lets you call 100+ AI model providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock, Azure and others) through one OpenAI-style interface.
BerriAI/litellm.why: It removes the need to learn a different SDK and request format for every provider, and the proxy adds team features such as virtual API keys, spend tracking, load balancing and guardrails. Developers and platform teams use it when an app or an organisation needs to switch between or share many models.
BerriAI/litellm.start: uv tool install 'litellm[proxy]' then litellm --model gpt-4o
BerriAI/litellm.caution: Aimed at developers and ops teams, not end users. Most of the code is open source, but some features are under a separate LiteLLM commercial/enterprise license (GitHub shows the license as NOASSERTION), so check which features you need before relying on them.
BerriAI/litellm.plain: A tool that lets one program talk to many different AI companies in the same way.
useFor: Call OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini models with the same code
Run one shared AI server for your whole team
Switch an app to a cheaper model without rewriting it
steps: Install the uv Python installer if you do not have it.
In a terminal, run `uv tool install 'litellm[proxy]'`.
Start the proxy with the model you want, as the README shows, and point your apps at it.
Check the license before relying on enterprise features, which are not all open source.

musistudio/claude-code-router.what: Claude Code Router (CCR) is a desktop app and CLI that runs a local gateway so Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and other coding agents can use models from providers you choose (DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Kimi, Gemini, etc.) through one local endpoint.
musistudio/claude-code-router.why: It lets you keep your usual coding agent but swap or mix the model behind it, with retries, fallback models, key rotation and request/cost logs. People reach for it to use cheaper or different models inside Claude Code, or to manage several agents' model settings in one place.
musistudio/claude-code-router.start: Download the desktop app from the Releases page, or: npm install -g @musistudio/claude-code-router && ccr ui
musistudio/claude-code-router.caution: The project is sponsored by Kimi and the README includes affiliate links. Using Claude Code with non-Anthropic models can behave differently than with Claude, and you still pay the providers you route to.
musistudio/claude-code-router.plain: A desktop app that lets Claude Code and similar tools use AI models from other, often cheaper, companies.
useFor: Run Claude Code on DeepSeek, Kimi or Gemini models
Send different kinds of tasks to different models
Manage all your AI provider keys in one place
steps: Download the desktop app from the project's Releases page on GitHub.
Add the AI providers you want to use and paste in their API keys.
Or, if you prefer a terminal, run `npm install -g @musistudio/claude-code-router` and open its settings screen.
Remember you still pay the providers you route to, and results may differ from Claude.

Portkey-AI/gateway.what: Portkey AI Gateway is an open-source server that routes requests from your app to many AI model providers through one OpenAI-compatible API, with retries, fallbacks, load balancing and configurable guardrails.
Portkey-AI/gateway.why: Developers use it to make AI apps more reliable (automatic retries and fallbacks) and to enforce rules on inputs and outputs without writing that logic themselves. It also includes a local log console and an MCP gateway.
Portkey-AI/gateway.caution: Speed and scale figures (<1ms latency, 10B tokens/day) are the company's claims. Portkey is a commercial company; some features (org management, governance) are in the paid enterprise version, and the README says a 2.0 release is in pre-release on a separate branch, while the main branch was last pushed in May 2026.
Portkey-AI/gateway.plain: A server between your app and AI companies that retries or switches providers when one fails.
useFor: Fall back to a second AI provider when the first is down
Spread requests across several providers to avoid limits
Add safety checks to what your app sends and receives
steps: Install Node.js, which includes the npx command.
In a terminal, run `npx @portkey-ai/gateway` to start the gateway on your computer.
Point your app's AI requests at the gateway instead of directly at the provider.
Note that some team and governance features are only in the paid version.

JuliusBrussee/caveman.what: Caveman is a skill (a rule file) that makes AI coding agents answer in very short 'caveman' sentences, plus an optional local proxy and middleware that shrink logs, test output and other text before the agent reads it.
JuliusBrussee/caveman.why: AI usage is billed per token, and agents often write long explanations and read large tool outputs. Caveman targets both sides to lower cost and reading time, while leaving code, commands and error messages unchanged.
JuliusBrussee/caveman.caution: The repo description's '65% of tokens' and the savings figures are the project's claims; its own README says it can cost more than it saves on short Q&A (the rule file adds ~1,000 input tokens per call) and does not help if you are billed per request. The skill is MIT, but the proxy runtime is under BSL-1.1 (not fully open source). Measure on your own workload.
JuliusBrussee/caveman.plain: An add-on rule that makes AI coding helpers reply in very short sentences to use fewer tokens.
useFor: Cut the length of your coding agent's replies
Shrink long logs and test output before the AI reads them
Stretch a usage limit further during long coding sessions
steps: Install Node.js so the npx command works.
In a terminal, run `npx skills add JuliusBrussee/caveman -g`.
Use your coding agent as usual; its replies become much shorter.
Compare your usage before and after, since short Q&A chats can cost more.

headroomlabs-ai/headroom.what: Headroom compresses what an AI agent reads (tool outputs, logs, JSON, files, retrieved documents) on your own machine before it is sent to the model, and is available as a Python/TypeScript library, a local proxy, an MCP server, or a one-command wrapper for coding agents.
headroomlabs-ai/headroom.why: Long tool outputs fill the context window and cost money; Headroom shrinks them and keeps the originals locally so the model can fetch the full text when it needs it. People use it when agents work with large logs, search results or JSON.
headroomlabs-ai/headroom.start: uv tool install --python 3.13 "headroom-ai[all]" then headroom wrap claude
headroomlabs-ai/headroom.caution: Savings depend heavily on content: the README's own benchmarks show about 21-57% on realistic agent tasks and 90%+ only on very repetitive JSON/logs, with little gain on prose. 'headroom wrap' also installs the Serena MCP server at user scope, which stays until you run 'headroom unwrap'.
headroomlabs-ai/headroom.plain: A tool on your computer that shrinks what your AI helper reads, so each request costs less.
useFor: Compress long logs and tool output before Claude Code reads them
Lower token costs on tasks with lots of repetitive data
Stretch a usage limit further during agent sessions
steps: Install the uv Python installer if you do not have it.
In a terminal, run `uv tool install --python 3.13 "headroom-ai[all]"`.
Then start Claude Code through Headroom with its wrap command, as the README shows.
Use its unwrap command later to remove the extra Serena add-on it installs.

DietrichGebert/ponytail.what: Ponytail is a skill/plugin for Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI and Cursor that tells the agent to write the least code that works: reuse existing code, the standard library or built-in platform features before adding new code or dependencies.
DietrichGebert/ponytail.why: AI agents tend to over-build (extra libraries, wrappers, boilerplate). Ponytail is for people who want smaller diffs that are easier to review, while keeping validation, error handling, security and accessibility.
DietrichGebert/ponytail.start: In Claude Code: /plugin marketplace add DietrichGebert/ponytail, then /plugin install ponytail@ponytail (as two separate prompts)
DietrichGebert/ponytail.caution: The -54% code / -20% cost numbers come from the author's own benchmark (12 tasks, one model, n=4); the README notes earlier, larger numbers were partly a measurement artifact. It is a prompt instruction, so results vary by model and task, and the always-on hooks need Node.js on your PATH.
DietrichGebert/ponytail.plain: An add-on that tells your AI coding helper to write as little new code as possible.
useFor: Get shorter, simpler code from Claude Code or Cursor
Stop the AI from adding libraries you do not need
Keep small fixes small instead of big rewrites
steps: Inside Claude Code, type `/plugin marketplace add DietrichGebert/ponytail`.
In a separate message, install the ponytail plugin from that marketplace, as the README shows.
Make sure Node.js is installed, since its always-on hooks need it.

ccusage/ccusage.what: ccusage is a command-line tool that reads the usage logs that coding agents store on your computer (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Copilot CLI and others) and shows tokens and estimated cost by day, week, month or session.
ccusage/ccusage.why: It answers 'how much am I actually using and what would it cost?' without sending anything to a service. It also shows Claude Code's 5-hour usage windows and can feed a status line.
ccusage/ccusage.caution: Costs are estimates calculated from local logs and published prices, not your actual bill; on flat-rate subscriptions the dollar figure is what the usage would have cost at API prices.
ccusage/ccusage.plain: A small tool that shows how many tokens and dollars your AI coding tools have used.
useFor: See what your Claude Code usage would cost this month
Compare token use across days, weeks or sessions
Check which coding agent uses the most tokens
steps: Install Node.js so the npx command works.
In a terminal, run `npx ccusage@latest`.
Read the daily totals, treating dollar amounts as estimates rather than your real bill.

gsd-build/get-shit-done.what: Get Shit Done (GSD) is a set of commands and agents that drive Claude Code and other coding agents through a fixed loop of discuss, plan, execute, verify and ship, one project phase at a time; this repository is archived and development continues as GSD Core in open-gsd/gsd-core.
gsd-build/get-shit-done.why: It targets 'context rot', where an agent's quality drops as a long session fills its context, by splitting work into planned phases that each run with a fresh context. People use it for multi-step projects where they want structure rather than one long chat.
gsd-build/get-shit-done.caution: This repo is archived and read-only; use open-gsd/gsd-core for current code, issues and releases. The phase loop adds ceremony that may be overkill for small changes.
gsd-build/get-shit-done.plain: A set of commands that walks your AI coding helper through plan, build, check and ship steps.
useFor: Plan a new app one phase at a time with Claude Code
Make the AI check its own work before moving on
Keep a larger project organized across many sessions
steps: Prefer an alternative: GSD Core (open-gsd/gsd-core), the maintained successor of this archived repo.
In a terminal, run `npx @opengsd/gsd-core@latest`.
Inside Claude Code, use the new-project command it adds to start planning.
Skip it for small changes, where the phase loop adds extra steps.

SuperClaude-Org/SuperClaude_Framework.what: SuperClaude is a configuration framework that installs about 30 '/sc:' slash commands, 20 agent personas and behaviour modes into Claude Code, covering tasks like brainstorming, research, implementation, testing and project management.
SuperClaude-Org/SuperClaude_Framework.why: It gives Claude Code a ready-made set of structured workflows so you do not have to write your own prompts for common development steps. People reach for it when they want a menu of commands rather than free-form prompting.
SuperClaude-Org/SuperClaude_Framework.start: pipx install superclaude then superclaude install
SuperClaude-Org/SuperClaude_Framework.caution: Not affiliated with Anthropic. The '2-3x faster, 30-50% fewer tokens' figures for optional MCP servers are the project's claims without shown measurements. The README says a plugin-based v5 is in development with no ETA, so older docs describing plugin install do not apply yet.
SuperClaude-Org/SuperClaude_Framework.plain: A pack of ready-made commands and helper personas added to Claude Code for common tasks.
useFor: Brainstorm a feature with a ready-made command
Ask Claude Code to research, test or review in a set style
Switch Claude Code into different working modes
steps: Install pipx, a tool for installing Python apps.
In a terminal, run `pipx install superclaude`.
Then run the SuperClaude install command so it adds its commands to Claude Code.
Inside Claude Code, look for the new commands that start with sc.

wshobson/agents.what: A large catalogue of installable plugins for Claude Code (also generated for Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Copilot, Antigravity and Pi) containing about 200 specialist sub-agents, 184 skills and 105 slash commands across programming languages, infrastructure, security and more.
wshobson/agents.why: Instead of writing your own specialist agents and commands, you install only the plugins you need (for example Python development), and only those load into the agent's context. It suits people who want domain-specific helpers on demand.
wshobson/agents.start: In Claude Code: /plugin marketplace add wshobson/agents, then /plugin install python-development
wshobson/agents.caution: Quality varies across so many components; the repo's own LLM-judge quality scoring is marked experimental. Some agents are configured for premium models (Opus, and an opt-in top tier), which can raise costs.
wshobson/agents.plain: A big catalog of add-ons that give Claude Code specialist helpers for languages, security and more.
useFor: Add a Python or JavaScript specialist helper to Claude Code
Run a security review with a ready-made agent
Pick only the skills and commands your project needs
steps: Inside Claude Code, type `/plugin marketplace add wshobson/agents`.
Then install only the plugin you need, such as python-development.
Check which model each agent uses, since premium models cost more.

davila7/claude-code-templates.what: Claude Code Templates is a CLI (with a browsable website, aitmpl.com) that installs ready-made agents, slash commands, hooks, settings, MCP integrations and skills into Claude Code, and also includes usage analytics, a conversation monitor and a health check.
davila7/claude-code-templates.why: It saves you from hand-writing Claude Code configuration: you pick components from a catalogue and install them with one command. It is useful when you want to try many community add-ons quickly or see what your Claude Code sessions are doing.
davila7/claude-code-templates.caution: Many components are collected from other repositories and third parties, each with its own license and quality; review agents, hooks and MCP servers before installing, since hooks run commands on your machine. The '--chats --tunnel' option exposes your conversations remotely through Cloudflare, so use it carefully.
davila7/claude-code-templates.plain: A tool and website for picking ready-made add-ons and settings and installing them into Claude Code.
useFor: Browse and install ready-made agents and commands
Add a connection to another app to Claude Code
Check your Claude Code setup and usage
steps: Browse the available components on the project's website to see what fits.
In a terminal, run `npx claude-code-templates@latest` and pick what to install.
Review hooks and connections before installing, since hooks run commands on your computer.
Be careful with the remote chat option, which exposes your conversations online.

obra/superpowers.what: Superpowers is a set of skills for coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and many others) that makes the agent follow a fixed method: brainstorm and agree a design with you, write a detailed plan, then implement it with test-driven development and sub-agents that review each task.
obra/superpowers.why: It stops the agent from jumping straight into code and makes it clarify what you want and plan first, which helps on larger features. The skills trigger automatically, so you use your agent as usual.
obra/superpowers.caution: The structured process (questions, design docs, plans, TDD, sub-agents) takes more time and tokens than a direct request and can feel heavy for small fixes. The README mentions long autonomous runs; keep an eye on usage.
obra/superpowers.plain: Add-on instructions that make your AI coding helper plan with you before it writes any code.
useFor: Agree on a design with the AI before it builds
Get a written step-by-step plan for a new feature
Have each finished task checked by a reviewer agent
steps: Inside Claude Code, type `/plugin install superpowers@claude-plugins-official`.
Describe what you want to build and answer the design questions it asks.
Approve the plan, then let it build and test step by step.
Skip it for tiny fixes, since the process takes more time and tokens.

NousResearch/hermes-agent.what: Hermes Agent is a general-purpose AI agent from Nous Research that runs in your terminal (and can connect to chat apps like Telegram or Discord), works with many model providers, and saves reusable skills and memories from past conversations.
NousResearch/hermes-agent.why: It is for people who want one personal assistant agent that remembers across sessions and gets tools like web search, browsing and messaging, without being tied to a single model vendor. You can switch models with one command.
NousResearch/hermes-agent.start: curl -fsSL https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.sh | bash (Windows: iex (irm https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.ps1)), then run hermes
NousResearch/hermes-agent.caution: The README's claim that it is 'the only agent with a built-in learning loop' is the project's own. The installer pulls in Python, Node.js and other tools, and the README notes some antivirus tools flag its bundled uv.exe as a false positive. It keeps memory of your conversations locally and gets broad tool access, so review what you enable; the optional Nous Portal is a paid subscription.
NousResearch/hermes-agent.plain: A personal AI assistant for your terminal or chat apps that remembers what it learns from you.
useFor: Chat with an AI assistant from Telegram or Discord
Save a repeated task as a skill it can reuse
Switch between different AI model providers
steps: In a terminal, run the one-line installer from the README; there is a separate Windows version.
Start it by typing `hermes` in a terminal.
Choose a model provider and review which tools and chat apps you enable.
If antivirus flags its bundled uv.exe, the README says this is a false alarm.

addyosmani/agent-skills.what: Agent Skills is a collection of 25 skills and 9 slash commands (/spec, /plan, /build, /test, /review, /ship and others) that package common senior-engineer practices for AI coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and Gemini CLI.
addyosmani/agent-skills.why: It makes an agent follow a consistent process across the whole development cycle: writing a spec first, small tasks, tests, code review and a pre-launch checklist. People use it to get more disciplined output from an agent without writing these instructions themselves.
addyosmani/agent-skills.caution: Skills are plain Markdown instructions, so how closely they are followed depends on the agent and model. The README notes that installing a single skill leaves out shared reference checklists, and that the Claude Code marketplace install can fail without GitHub SSH keys (an HTTPS workaround is given).
addyosmani/agent-skills.plain: A collection of add-on instructions that make AI coding helpers follow good engineering habits.
useFor: Write a clear spec before the AI starts coding
Have the AI review its changes like a senior engineer
Follow a checklist before shipping a feature
steps: Install Node.js so the npx command works.
In a terminal, run `npx skills add addyosmani/agent-skills`.
In your coding agent, try its new spec, plan, build, test and review commands.

anthropics/claude-code.what: Anthropic's official coding assistant that runs in your terminal (and in IDEs or via @claude on GitHub) and reads, edits and runs code in your project from plain-language requests.
anthropics/claude-code.why: Use it when you want an AI to do hands-on work in a real codebase, such as making changes across files, explaining unfamiliar code or handling git tasks, instead of copy-pasting into a chat window.
anthropics/claude-code.start: curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash   (Windows: irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex), then run `claude` inside your project folder
anthropics/claude-code.caution: Not open source: this repo holds docs, plugins and the issue tracker, and GitHub shows no license. It needs a paid Claude plan or API key. The README says Anthropic collects usage and conversation data as feedback; read the data-usage policy. It can edit files and run commands, so review what it does.
anthropics/claude-code.plain: Anthropic's AI assistant that reads and changes the code in your project when you ask in plain words.
useFor: Fix a bug by describing it in plain words
Build a small website or tool from an idea
Get an explanation of how an unfamiliar project works
steps: Get a paid Claude plan or an API key, since it needs one.
Install it with the one-line command from the README for Mac, Linux or Windows.
Open a terminal in your project folder and type `claude`.
Ask for changes in plain words and review what it edits or runs.

openai/codex.what: Codex CLI is OpenAI's coding agent that runs locally in your terminal. It is also available as an IDE extension and a desktop app.
openai/codex.why: Use it if you already pay for ChatGPT and want an agent that reads and changes code on your computer. The README recommends signing in with a ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, Edu or Enterprise account.
openai/codex.start: npm install -g @openai/codex, then run `codex` and choose Sign in with ChatGPT
openai/codex.caution: Usage counts against your ChatGPT plan, or you can bill an API key, which needs extra setup. The CLI is Apache-2.0 open source, but the models run on OpenAI's servers, so your code is sent there.
openai/codex.plain: OpenAI's AI helper that runs in your terminal and writes or fixes code in your project.
useFor: Fix a bug by describing it in plain words
Add a new feature to an existing project
Use your ChatGPT plan for coding help
steps: Install Node.js, which includes the npm installer.
In a terminal, run `npm install -g @openai/codex`.
Start Codex from your project folder and choose Sign in with ChatGPT.
Remember your code is sent to OpenAI's servers.

google-gemini/gemini-cli.what: Google's open-source (Apache-2.0) AI agent for the terminal. It uses Gemini models and can work with files, run shell commands, search Google and fetch web pages.
google-gemini/gemini-cli.why: It is a low-cost way to try a terminal agent. The README lists a free tier of 60 requests per minute and 1,000 per day when you sign in with a personal Google account, and it can also run non-interactively in scripts and GitHub workflows.
google-gemini/gemini-cli.caution: The free-tier limits and model access come from Google's terms and can change. Prompts and code go to Google's servers. Preview and nightly releases are described as not fully vetted, so stay on the stable (latest) tag.
google-gemini/gemini-cli.plain: Google's free AI helper for your terminal that works with files, runs commands and searches the web.
useFor: Fix or explain code in a project folder
Search Google and summarize web pages from the terminal
Rename or sort files by describing what you want
steps: Install Node.js so the npx command works.
In a terminal, run `npx @google/gemini-cli`.
Sign in with your Google account when it asks.
Stay on the stable release, since preview and nightly builds are less tested.

anomalyco/opencode.what: An MIT-licensed AI coding agent with a terminal interface and a beta desktop app. It comes with a full-access 'build' agent and a read-only 'plan' agent that you switch between with Tab.
anomalyco/opencode.why: Use it if you want an open-source alternative to vendor coding CLIs. The read-only plan mode is useful for exploring an unfamiliar codebase before letting the AI change anything.
anomalyco/opencode.caution: The desktop app is labeled beta. The README says little about model setup; you still need your own model provider or account, which is covered in the external docs.
anomalyco/opencode.plain: A free, open-source AI coding helper for your terminal that can plan changes or edit your code.
useFor: Plan a change safely with the read-only plan agent
Let the build agent edit and fix your code
Use the AI model provider you already pay for
steps: Install Node.js, which includes the npm installer.
In a terminal, run `npm i -g opencode-ai@latest`.
Connect your own model provider or account, following the external docs.
Press Tab to switch between the read-only plan agent and the build agent.

cline/cline.what: An open-source coding agent that runs as a VS Code extension, a JetBrains plugin, a CLI and a desktop app. It edits files and runs terminal commands, asking for your approval on each step by default.
cline/cline.why: Use it when you want an agent inside your editor that shows every change as a reviewable diff, works with many model providers (including local ones via Ollama or LM Studio), and has a Plan mode for agreeing on an approach first.
cline/cline.start: Install the Cline extension from the VS Code Marketplace (or run npm i -g cline for the CLI)
cline/cline.caution: You pay your chosen model provider directly, and long agent sessions can use a lot of tokens. Auto-approve lets it run commands unattended, so use it with care. The JetBrains plugin is not open source.
cline/cline.plain: A free VS Code add-on that lets an AI edit your files and run commands, asking you first.
useFor: Build a feature by chatting inside your code editor
Fix errors while approving each step the AI takes
Use the AI model provider you already have
steps: Open VS Code and install the Cline extension from the Marketplace.
Choose a model provider and add your API key or account.
Describe a task in the Cline panel and approve each step it proposes.
Avoid auto-approve until you trust it, and keep an eye on token costs.

OpenHands/OpenHands.what: OpenHands Agent Canvas is a self-hosted web app for running and managing coding agents: its own OpenHands agent, or Claude Code, Codex and Gemini through the ACP protocol. Agents can run locally, in Docker, on VMs or in the cloud.
OpenHands/OpenHands.why: Use it to run coding agents as an always-on service, for example scheduled reports to Slack or turning GitHub issues into tasks, rather than one person chatting in a terminal.
OpenHands/OpenHands.start: npm install -g @openhands/agent-canvas, then run `agent-canvas` and open http://localhost:8000
OpenHands/OpenHands.caution: The README warns that the non-Docker install gives the agent full access to your filesystem; use the Docker sandbox option if you are unsure. Server setup needs care with network exposure and security hardening (see SELF_HOSTING.md). The repo has recently been refocused as 'Agent Canvas', so older guides may not match.
OpenHands/OpenHands.plain: A web app you run yourself to start and manage several AI coding helpers in one place.
useFor: Run Claude Code, Codex and Gemini side by side
Keep coding agents inside a safe Docker sandbox
Watch and manage long-running coding tasks from a browser
steps: Install Node.js, which includes the npm installer.
In a terminal, run `npm install -g @openhands/agent-canvas`.
Start agent-canvas, then open localhost port 8000 in your browser.
Choose the Docker sandbox option so agents cannot reach all your files.

Aider-AI/aider.what: An open-source (Apache-2.0) tool for pair programming with an AI in your terminal. It maps your codebase, edits files and commits each change to git automatically.
Aider-AI/aider.why: Use it if you want a coding assistant that works with almost any model, including local ones, and that commits every AI edit to git so you can inspect or undo it with normal git tools.
Aider-AI/aider.start: python -m pip install aider-install && aider-install, then in your project: aider --model sonnet --api-key anthropic=<key>
Aider-AI/aider.caution: Last push was 22 May 2026, more than four months ago, so development may have slowed. The README's recommended models (Claude 3.7 Sonnet, GPT-4o, o3-mini) are out of date. You need your own API key, and costs depend on the model you pick.
Aider-AI/aider.plain: An AI pair programmer in your terminal that edits your code and saves each change in git.
useFor: Ask for code changes and get each one saved in git
Refactor several files in a project at once
Undo an AI change easily through git history
steps: Get an API key from a model provider such as Anthropic.
In a terminal, run `python -m pip install aider-install && aider-install`.
In your project folder, start aider with your model and API key, as the README shows.
Choose a current model, since the README's suggested models are out of date.

aaif-goose/goose.what: An open-source (Apache-2.0) AI agent written in Rust that runs on your machine as a desktop app, CLI or API. It is for coding and also for research, writing and automation.
aaif-goose/goose.why: Use it if you want a general assistant that is not limited to code, can use 15+ model providers or an existing Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini subscription, and connects to external tools through MCP extensions.
aaif-goose/goose.start: Download the desktop app from goose-docs.ai, or run: curl -fsSL https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/releases/download/stable/download_cli.sh | bash
aaif-goose/goose.caution: The README is short, so most setup details are in external docs. An agent that can run commands and use many extensions can change things on your computer; only add extensions you trust.
aaif-goose/goose.plain: A free AI assistant app for your computer that helps with coding, research, writing and automation.
useFor: Automate a repetitive task on your computer
Research a topic and draft a write-up
Build or fix code in a project folder
steps: Download the desktop app from the goose docs website.
Set up a model provider, following the external docs.
Add only extensions you trust, since it can run commands on your computer.

continuedev/continue.what: Continue is an open-source coding agent for VS Code, JetBrains and the command line. Its makers have stopped developing it after a final 2.0.0 release.
continuedev/continue.why: It was one of the early open-source AI assistants inside the editor. Today it is mainly useful as a finished, frozen tool or as a codebase for others to build on.
continuedev/continue.start: Install 'Continue' from the VS Code Marketplace
continuedev/continue.caution: The README says the repo is no longer actively maintained and is read-only, so no bug fixes or new model support are coming. For new users, an actively maintained alternative is safer. The final release removed telemetry and built-in authentication.
continuedev/continue.plain: A free AI coding add-on for VS Code and JetBrains that is no longer being developed.
useFor: Chat about code inside VS Code
Ask the AI to edit a file you have open
Keep using an existing setup while you switch tools
steps: Prefer an alternative: Cline is an actively maintained coding agent for VS Code.
If you still want it, install Continue from the VS Code Marketplace.
Expect no bug fixes or new model support from now on.

RooCodeInc/Roo-Code.what: Roo Code was a VS Code extension, forked from Cline, that offered AI agents in modes such as Code, Architect, Ask and Debug. The README says the extension was shut down on 15 May 2026 and the repository is archived.
RooCodeInc/Roo-Code.why: It is listed here only for context. Former users are pointed to the community fork ZooCode or back to Cline.
RooCodeInc/Roo-Code.caution: Discontinued: the product was shut down on 15 May 2026, and the repo is archived with no updates since then. Do not start new work with it.
RooCodeInc/Roo-Code.plain: A former AI coding add-on for VS Code that was shut down in May 2026.
useFor: Move an existing Roo Code setup to a maintained tool
Study how an editor agent with modes was built
Look up how its Code, Architect and Debug modes worked
steps: Prefer an alternative: Cline, the tool Roo Code was forked from, is still maintained.
Do not start new work with Roo Code; the product is shut down and the repo archived.
Move existing projects to Cline or another maintained editor agent.

langchain-ai/langgraph.what: A low-level Python library (with a JS version) from LangChain Inc for building long-running, stateful AI agents as graphs of steps.
langchain-ai/langgraph.why: Use it when you are writing code for an agent that has to survive crashes and resume where it stopped, pause for human approval, or keep memory across sessions. For a quicker start, the README points to its higher-level 'Deep Agents' package.
langchain-ai/langgraph.caution: It is intentionally low-level, so expect a learning curve. The README steers you toward LangChain's paid LangSmith tracing and deployment services, but the MIT-licensed library works without them.
langchain-ai/langgraph.plain: A Python toolkit for programmers to build AI helpers that work through many steps over time.
useFor: Build an agent that follows a multi-step business process
Pause an AI workflow for human approval, then resume
Keep an agent's progress saved across long tasks
steps: Install Python if you do not have it.
In a terminal, run `pip install -U langgraph`.
Follow the README quickstart to build a small agent in Python.
The paid LangSmith services are optional; the library works without them.

crewAIInc/crewAI.what: An open-source (MIT) Python framework for building teams of AI agents with roles (Crews) and step-by-step, event-driven workflows (Flows).
crewAIInc/crewAI.why: Use it when a task splits naturally into roles, such as a researcher, a writer and a reviewer, and you want those agents to cooperate in code. It includes a CLI that scaffolds a project for you.
crewAIInc/crewAI.start: uv tool install crewai, then crewai create crew <project_name>
crewAIInc/crewAI.caution: You need Python between 3.10 and 3.13 and your own model API keys. Anonymous telemetry is on by default; set OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true to turn it off. The README also promotes a paid enterprise suite (AMP). Its 'becoming the standard' claim is the project's own.
crewAIInc/crewAI.plain: A Python toolkit for building a team of AI helpers, each with its own role.
useFor: Build a researcher and a writer agent that work together
Automate a report that needs several steps
Run a step-by-step AI workflow triggered by events
steps: Install Python 3.10 to 3.13 and get an API key for your model provider.
In a terminal, run `uv tool install crewai`.
Create a starter crew project with its create command, as the README shows.
Turn off the anonymous telemetry with the setting the README names, if you prefer.

openai/openai-agents-python.what: OpenAI's MIT-licensed Python SDK for building agents and multi-agent workflows, with tools, handoffs between agents, guardrails, sessions, tracing, and voice or realtime agents.
openai/openai-agents-python.why: Use it when you are writing Python and want a fairly small, official toolkit to build agents. The README says it also works with 100+ non-OpenAI models, not only OpenAI's.
openai/openai-agents-python.start: pip install openai-agents (Python 3.10+), then set OPENAI_API_KEY
openai/openai-agents-python.caution: It is a library for developers, not an app. The sandbox example's local client works only on macOS and Linux; Windows needs Docker or a hosted sandbox. Although it is provider-agnostic, it is designed around OpenAI's APIs first.
openai/openai-agents-python.plain: OpenAI's Python toolkit for programmers to build AI helpers that use tools and hand off work.
useFor: Build a support bot that hands tricky questions to a specialist
Give an AI agent tools it can call from your code
Build a voice agent that answers questions out loud
steps: Install Python 3.10 or newer and get an OpenAI API key.
In a terminal, run `pip install openai-agents`.
Save your key as the OPENAI_API_KEY setting, then try a README example.
On Windows, use Docker or a hosted sandbox for the sandbox example.

anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python.what: Anthropic's MIT-licensed Python SDK that lets your own program drive Claude Code, with its file, edit and shell tools, plus custom tools and hooks that you write in Python.
anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python.why: Use it when you want to build your own agent or automation on the same engine as Claude Code, for example a bot that edits files in a repo, without building the agent loop yourself.
anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python.caution: By default the agent has the full Claude Code toolset, including Bash and file writes, so set allowed_tools and permission_mode deliberately. It bundles the Claude Code CLI and needs Claude access, which is billed. Some options require specific CLI versions.
anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python.plain: Anthropic's Python toolkit that lets your own program use Claude Code to read, edit and run things.
useFor: Run Claude Code tasks automatically from a Python script
Give Claude custom tools written in Python
Build a helper that edits files in a set folder
steps: Make sure you have Python and paid Claude access.
In a terminal, run `pip install claude-agent-sdk`.
Write a short Python script that sends Claude a task, following the README.
Limit which tools it may use, since it can run commands by default.

microsoft/autogen.what: Microsoft's Python framework for building multi-agent AI applications. It includes AutoGen Studio, a no-code GUI.
microsoft/autogen.why: It was a popular early framework for agents that talk to each other. Microsoft now tells new users to start with its successor, Microsoft Agent Framework, and existing users to migrate.
microsoft/autogen.caution: In maintenance mode: no new features, and it is community-managed. The last push was 15 April 2026, more than four months ago. GitHub lists the repository license as CC-BY-4.0. The README warns that MCP servers can run commands on your machine, so connect only to trusted ones.
microsoft/autogen.plain: Microsoft's older Python toolkit for building teams of AI helpers, now only lightly maintained.
useFor: Build a group of AI agents that talk to each other
Prototype a multi-agent workflow in the AutoGen Studio app
Maintain an existing AutoGen project
steps: Prefer an alternative: the README tells new users to start with Microsoft Agent Framework.
If you still need it, in a terminal run `pip install -U "autogen-agentchat" "autogen-ext[openai]"`.
Connect only trusted MCP servers, since they can run commands on your machine.

vercel/ai.what: The AI SDK is Vercel's free TypeScript library for adding AI to web apps. It gives one API across OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and others, plus UI hooks for building chat interfaces in React, Next.js, Svelte and Vue.
vercel/ai.why: Use it if you build JavaScript or TypeScript web apps and want to generate text, structured data or tool-using agents without writing separate code for each AI provider.
vercel/ai.caution: By default, model strings are routed through Vercel's AI Gateway, a Vercel service. Install the provider packages (such as @ai-sdk/openai) to call providers directly. It needs Node.js 22+. The LICENSE file is Apache-2.0, although GitHub does not detect it.
vercel/ai.plain: A JavaScript toolkit for adding AI chat and features to websites, working with many AI companies.
useFor: Add a chat box to a Next.js or React website
Switch your app between OpenAI, Anthropic and Google models
Stream AI answers into a web page as they are written
steps: Install Node.js 22 or newer.
In your web project's folder, in a terminal, run `npm install ai`.
Add a provider package, such as the OpenAI one, to call that provider directly.
Without one, requests go through Vercel's AI Gateway service by default.

browser-use/browser-use.what: An open-source (MIT) Python library and CLI that lets an AI agent operate a web browser: clicking, filling in forms and navigating sites to finish a task you describe in words. The company also sells a hosted cloud version.
browser-use/browser-use.why: Use it to automate web tasks that have no API, such as looking something up across sites or filling in forms, by describing the goal instead of writing browser scripts.
browser-use/browser-use.start: uv add browser-use (Python 3.11+), add OPENAI_API_KEY to .env, then run the README's agent.py example
browser-use/browser-use.caution: An agent acting in a browser that is logged into your accounts can take real actions, so supervise it and avoid sensitive sessions. The README shows it solving CAPTCHAs, which may break some websites' terms. Cloud browsers and the BU2 model are paid services.
browser-use/browser-use.plain: A Python tool that lets an AI click, type and move around websites to finish a task for you.
useFor: Fill in a long web form from your notes
Collect prices or facts from several websites
Repeat a routine task on a website automatically
steps: Install Python 3.11 or newer and get an OpenAI API key.
In your project folder, in a terminal, run `uv add browser-use`.
Put your API key in a .env file and run the README's agent.py example.
Watch it closely and keep it away from browsers logged into sensitive accounts.

ollama/ollama.what: A desktop app and command-line tool that downloads open-weight AI models (Gemma, Qwen, DeepSeek, gpt-oss and others) and runs them on your own computer.
ollama/ollama.why: Use it when you want to chat with an AI model offline or privately, or give other apps a local model through its built-in API on localhost:11434. It can also launch tools like Claude Code or Codex pointed at a local model with `ollama launch`.
ollama/ollama.start: Install from ollama.com/download, then run `ollama run gemma4`
ollama/ollama.caution: Local models are usually less capable than top cloud models, and larger ones need a lot of RAM or GPU memory. The quick-install command pipes a script from the internet into your shell; use the manual installer if you prefer to check first.
ollama/ollama.plain: A free app that runs AI chatbots on your own computer, so your chats stay private.
useFor: Chat with an AI model without sending data online
Try open models like Gemma, Qwen or DeepSeek
Power other local AI apps with models on your computer
steps: Download and install Ollama from the official Ollama website.
In a terminal, run `ollama run gemma4` to download a model and start chatting.
Start with smaller models if your computer has little memory.

ggml-org/llama.cpp.what: A C/C++ program that runs AI language and vision models on ordinary hardware (CPU, Apple Silicon, NVIDIA/AMD/Intel GPUs) and is the engine many other local-AI tools build on.
ggml-org/llama.cpp.why: Reach for it when you want direct, fine-grained control over running a model locally, or a lightweight OpenAI-compatible server with a built-in web UI (`llama serve`). Its compressed (quantized) model formats let larger models fit in less memory.
ggml-org/llama.cpp.caution: Lower-level than Ollama: you pick model files and settings yourself, and getting the best GPU speed may require the right build or compiling from source.
ggml-org/llama.cpp.plain: The engine behind many local AI apps; it runs AI models on ordinary computers without the cloud.
useFor: Chat with a small AI model on a laptop without internet
Run a local AI server that other apps can use
Test how fast different models run on your hardware
steps: Download a ready-made build from the Releases page, or follow the project website's instructions.
In a terminal, run `llama cli -hf ggml-org/Qwen3.5-0.8B-GGUF` to download and chat with a small model.
Use its serve command instead to run a local server with a built-in web chat.

open-webui/open-webui.what: A ChatGPT-style web interface you host yourself, connecting to local models via Ollama or to any OpenAI-compatible API.
open-webui/open-webui.why: Use it when you want one browser-based chat app for local and cloud models, with extras like document chat (RAG), web search, voice, multiple users and permissions. Common pairing: Ollama for the models, Open WebUI for the interface.
open-webui/open-webui.start: pip install open-webui, then run `open-webui serve`
open-webui/open-webui.caution: Not a standard open-source license: current code is under the 'Open WebUI License', which requires keeping the Open WebUI branding (GitHub lists it as unclassified). The feature list is very large, so expect a lot of settings; secure it properly before exposing it to the internet.
open-webui/open-webui.plain: A ChatGPT-style chat website you run yourself, connected to local or online AI models.
useFor: Give your team a private ChatGPT-style chat page
Chat with local Ollama models in a friendly window
Ask questions about uploaded documents
steps: Install Python 3.11, which the README recommends.
In a terminal, run `pip install open-webui`.
Start it with its serve command and open it in your browser.
Connect it to Ollama or an online AI service, and secure it before exposing it online.

vllm-project/vllm.what: A Python library and server from UC Berkeley's Sky Computing Lab for running open-weight models at high speed on GPUs, serving many requests at once through an OpenAI-compatible API.
vllm-project/vllm.why: Reach for it when you need to serve a model to many users or apps from your own GPU servers and care about throughput and memory efficiency. It is aimed at production serving rather than casual desktop chatting.
vllm-project/vllm.caution: Built for server-grade GPUs and Python environments; it is not a point-and-click app. For a single user on a laptop, Ollama or llama.cpp are simpler.
vllm-project/vllm.plain: Software that runs open AI models very fast on powerful graphics cards for many users at once.
useFor: Serve an open model to a whole team from one server
Replace a paid AI service with your own hardware
Handle many AI requests at once without slowing down
steps: Use a machine with a strong graphics card and Python installed.
In a terminal, run `uv pip install vllm`.
Start its server with a model name and connect apps to its OpenAI-style address.
For one person on a laptop, Ollama or llama.cpp are simpler.

mudler/LocalAI.what: A self-hosted server that runs text, image, voice and video models on your own hardware and exposes them through APIs compatible with OpenAI, Anthropic and ElevenLabs.
mudler/LocalAI.why: Use it when you want a single local stand-in for cloud AI APIs so existing apps can switch to self-hosted models. It downloads the right engine (llama.cpp, vLLM, whisper.cpp, etc.) only when a model needs it, and it also works without a GPU.
mudler/LocalAI.caution: Docker is the main install route. The macOS app is not signed by Apple (the README gives a workaround command). The built-in terminal agent can read files and run commands on your machine, but asks for approval before changing anything.
mudler/LocalAI.plain: A program you run on your own hardware that provides text, image and voice AI without the cloud.
useFor: Generate images and voices without an online service
Replace OpenAI in your apps with models on your own machine
Chat with local models through a web page
steps: Install Docker, the main way to run LocalAI.
In a terminal, run `docker run -ti --name local-ai -p 8080:8080 localai/localai:latest`.
Open localhost port 8080 in your browser to pick and try models.
On a Mac, follow the README's workaround, since the app is not signed by Apple.

Mintplex-Labs/anything-llm.what: A desktop and Docker app for chatting with your documents and running AI agents, using either local models or cloud providers like OpenAI or Anthropic.
Mintplex-Labs/anything-llm.why: Use it when you want a private 'ChatGPT over my files' without assembling the parts yourself: it includes document ingestion, a built-in vector database, agents, MCP support and multi-user workspaces. The desktop download makes it one of the easier ways to start.
Mintplex-Labs/anything-llm.start: Download the desktop app from anythingllm.com/download
Mintplex-Labs/anything-llm.caution: Anonymous telemetry is on by default; turn it off in Settings > Privacy or with DISABLE_TELEMETRY=true. Multi-user and the embeddable website widget are Docker-only. Claims such as 'up to 80% fewer tokens' come from the project and have not been independently checked.
Mintplex-Labs/anything-llm.plain: A desktop app for chatting with your own documents using local or online AI models.
useFor: Ask questions about a folder of PDFs and Word files
Keep document chats on your computer with a local model
Run simple AI agents that search and summarize
steps: Download the desktop app from the AnythingLLM website.
Pick a local model or connect a cloud provider such as OpenAI or Anthropic.
Add your documents to a workspace and ask questions about them.
Turn off anonymous telemetry under Settings, then Privacy.

mem0ai/mem0.what: A library, self-hosted server and paid cloud service that gives AI assistants long-term memory, storing facts about users and sessions and finding the relevant ones later.
mem0ai/mem0.why: Reach for it when you are building a chatbot or agent that should remember preferences and history across conversations instead of starting fresh every time. It is available for Python and JavaScript, plus a command-line tool.
mem0ai/mem0.caution: The headline benchmark scores come from Mem0's managed cloud platform, which the README says includes proprietary optimizations not in the open-source version. By default it uses OpenAI models, so your data is sent to OpenAI unless you configure a different provider. The 'sign up as an agent' quickstart creates a cloud account.
mem0ai/mem0.plain: A toolkit that gives AI assistants long-term memory, so they remember facts about each user.
useFor: Make your chatbot remember each customer's preferences
Recall past sessions when a user comes back
Add memory to an AI agent you are building
steps: Install Python and get an API key for your model provider.
In a terminal, run `pip install mem0ai`.
Follow the README example to add and search memories from your code.
Set a provider other than OpenAI if you do not want your data sent there.

getzep/graphiti.what: A Python framework that builds a knowledge graph from conversations and data, recording facts as connections between people, things and ideas, along with when each fact was true.
getzep/graphiti.why: Use it when an agent needs memory that handles changing facts (for example, 'lived in Paris until 2025') and can trace each fact back to its source, rather than just searching text chunks. It is the open-source core of Zep's commercial product.
getzep/graphiti.caution: You must run a graph database yourself (Neo4j, FalkorDB or Amazon Neptune) and supply an LLM API key. The README notes that production features like dashboards, user management and tuned performance are in the paid Zep service. The speed comparisons with GraphRAG are the project's own.
getzep/graphiti.plain: A Python toolkit that turns conversations and data into a map of facts that remembers when each was true.
useFor: Track how facts about customers change over time
Give an AI agent memory of people, things and events
Search connected facts instead of plain text
steps: Set up a graph database such as Neo4j and get an LLM API key.
In a terminal, run `pip install graphiti-core`.
Follow the README quickstart to add conversations and search the resulting graph.

Graphify-Labs/graphify.what: A command-line tool and /graphify skill for AI coding assistants that turns a project's code, docs, PDFs and media into a clickable, queryable knowledge graph.
Graphify-Labs/graphify.why: Use it when you or your coding assistant need to understand a large or unfamiliar codebase: it maps which parts call and import each other and lets you ask questions or trace how two things connect, instead of searching file by file. It works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI and others.
Graphify-Labs/graphify.start: uv tool install graphifyy, then run `graphify install`, then type `/graphify .` in your AI assistant
Graphify-Labs/graphify.caution: The package name is 'graphifyy' (two y's), so type it carefully. Code is parsed locally, but docs, PDFs, images and video go to your assistant's model or a configured API. The company is building a paid hosted platform, and its benchmark figures are self-reported.
Graphify-Labs/graphify.plain: A tool that turns a project's code and documents into a clickable map your AI assistant can search.
useFor: See how the files in a large project connect
Ask your AI assistant questions about a codebase
Map a folder of docs and PDFs into one graph
steps: Install the uv Python installer if you do not have it.
In a terminal, run `uv tool install graphifyy` (note the two y's).
Then run graphify's install command to add it to your AI assistant.
Inside your AI assistant, run the graphify command on your project folder.

run-llama/llama_index.what: A Python framework for connecting AI models to your own data (PDFs, databases, APIs) so they can search it and answer from it, a technique called RAG, and for building agents on top.
run-llama/llama_index.why: Reach for it when you are writing code for an app that answers questions over private documents and want ready-made pieces for loading, indexing and retrieval. It offers 300+ integration packages for different models and vector databases.
run-llama/llama_index.caution: The README says the company's main focus has moved to its paid LlamaParse cloud platform; the open-source framework is still available, but the README is updated less often than the docs. Picking among hundreds of integration packages can be confusing.
run-llama/llama_index.plain: A Python toolkit for letting AI search your own files and data and answer from them.
useFor: Turn a folder of PDFs into a searchable Q&A
Connect an AI to a company database
Build an agent that looks things up in your documents
steps: Install Python and get an API key for your model provider.
In a terminal, run `pip install llama-index`.
Follow the docs' starter example to load files and ask questions about them.

infiniflow/ragflow.what: A self-hosted platform that ingests documents (Word, Excel, slides, scans, web pages), splits and indexes them, and lets AI answer questions with citations back to the source.
infiniflow/ragflow.why: Use it when an organization wants a full 'chat with our documents' system that handles hard-to-read files through its own layout analysis, OCR and table recognition, and shows which passages each answer came from. A hosted cloud version is also offered.
infiniflow/ragflow.start: git clone https://github.com/infiniflow/ragflow.git, then in ragflow/docker run `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml up -d`
infiniflow/ragflow.caution: Heavy setup: the README recommends 4 CPU cores, 16 GB RAM, 50 GB disk and Docker. Version 1.0.0 is at release-candidate stage (rc1, September 2026). Words like 'leading' and 'superior' are the project's own description.
infiniflow/ragflow.plain: A system you host yourself that reads your documents and answers questions with sources cited.
useFor: Ask questions about Word, Excel and scanned files
Get answers that point back to the source page
Build a private company knowledge base
steps: Use a machine with Docker, 4 CPU cores, 16 GB RAM and 50 GB free disk.
Download the project with git clone, as the README shows.
In the ragflow/docker folder, in a terminal, run `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml up -d`.
Open the web interface, upload documents and ask questions.

microsoft/markitdown.what: A Python tool from Microsoft that converts PDFs, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, HTML, images, audio and more into Markdown text that AI models can read easily.
microsoft/markitdown.why: Use it when you need to feed documents to an AI or a RAG pipeline and want clean text that keeps headings, lists and tables. It runs from the command line (`markitdown file.pdf -o file.md`) or from Python.
microsoft/markitdown.caution: It reads files and URLs with your user's full permissions, so the README warns to sanitize inputs in untrusted settings. Built-in converters are basic for scanned PDFs, images and video; better results need the OCR plugin (which calls an LLM) or paid Azure services.
microsoft/markitdown.plain: A Microsoft tool that turns PDFs, Word, Excel and slides into plain text that AI reads easily.
useFor: Turn a Word or PDF file into text for a chatbot
Convert slides or spreadsheets into readable Markdown
Prepare a pile of documents for AI search
steps: Install Python if you do not have it.
In a terminal, run `pip install 'markitdown[all]'`.
Point markitdown at a file in the terminal to get its text as Markdown.
Only convert files you trust, since it reads with your full permissions.

n8n-io/n8n.what: A visual workflow builder, similar to Zapier, that connects apps and services (1500+ integrations) and can include AI models and agents as steps, run self-hosted or in n8n's cloud.
n8n-io/n8n.why: Reach for it when you want to automate business processes, such as 'when an email arrives, summarize it with AI and post it to Slack', by dragging nodes on a canvas, with optional JavaScript or Python for custom logic.
n8n-io/n8n.caution: Not open source in the OSI sense: it is 'fair-code' under the Sustainable Use License, which limits some commercial uses (for example, reselling it as a hosted service), and some features need a paid Enterprise License. Read the license before building a business on it.
n8n-io/n8n.plain: A visual tool, like Zapier, for linking apps into automatic workflows that can include AI steps.
useFor: Summarize new emails with AI and post them to chat
Copy form entries into a spreadsheet automatically
Run an AI agent on a schedule
steps: Install Docker, which the n8n installer needs.
In a terminal, run `curl -fsSL https://get.n8n.io | sh`.
Open n8n in your browser and build a workflow by connecting app blocks.
Read the Sustainable Use License before building a business on it.

langgenius/dify.what: A web platform for building AI apps (chatbots, agents, document-search assistants and multi-step workflows) on a visual canvas, run in Dify's cloud or self-hosted with Docker.
langgenius/dify.why: Use it when a team wants to prototype and ship AI apps without writing all the plumbing: it bundles workflows, RAG over your documents, a prompt editor, logs and monitoring, and an API for each app. It supports hundreds of models from many providers.
langgenius/dify.start: git clone https://github.com/langgenius/dify.git, then in dify/docker run `cp .env.example .env` and `docker compose up -d`
langgenius/dify.caution: The license is the 'Dify Open Source License', which is Apache 2.0 with additional conditions, not plain Apache; check it before offering Dify as a service. Self-hosting needs Docker and at least 2 CPU cores and 4 GB RAM.
langgenius/dify.plain: A website for building AI apps like chatbots and document helpers by connecting blocks on a canvas.
useFor: Build a chatbot that answers from your documents
Design a multi-step AI workflow without code
Share a finished AI app with your team
steps: Install Docker on a machine with at least 2 CPU cores and 4 GB RAM.
Download the project with git clone and copy the example settings file, as the README shows.
In the dify/docker folder, in a terminal, run `docker compose up -d`.
Open Dify in your browser and build your first app on the canvas.

FlowiseAI/Flowise.what: A drag-and-drop tool for building AI chatbots, agents and RAG flows by connecting blocks on a canvas, built on LangChain components.
FlowiseAI/Flowise.why: People used it to build AI assistants visually and expose them as an API or website chat widget without much coding. It installs with npm or Docker.
FlowiseAI/Flowise.start: npm install -g flowise, then run `npx flowise start`
FlowiseAI/Flowise.caution: The repository has been archived by its maintainers (read-only, no further updates); see the 'Future of Flowise' discussion. Avoid it for new projects and look at maintained alternatives. The code is Apache 2.0.
FlowiseAI/Flowise.plain: A drag-and-drop tool for building AI chatbots from blocks, now archived by its makers.
useFor: Build a chatbot by connecting blocks on a canvas
Make a bot that answers from your documents
Keep an existing Flowise project running
steps: Prefer an alternative: Dify is a maintained visual builder for AI apps.
If you still want to try it, in a terminal run `npm install -g flowise`.
Start Flowise with its start command and open it in your browser.
Expect no further updates or fixes, since the repo is read-only.

lobehub/lobehub.what: A self-hostable web app for chatting with many AI models and organizing multiple AI 'agents' into teams that can run on schedules, share context and use plugins and MCP tools.
lobehub/lobehub.why: Use it when you want a polished chat interface for several model providers, plus features such as scheduled agent runs, group agents, personal memory and a plugin library, either on its hosted service or on your own server.
lobehub/lobehub.caution: It is under the 'LobeHub Community License', which GitHub cannot classify as a standard open-source license (the badge says Apache 2.0, but the README text names the custom license), so check the terms before commercial use. The README says it is under active development. Phrases like 'Chief Agent Operator' and '10,000+ skills' are the project's own marketing.
lobehub/lobehub.plain: A chat website you can host yourself to talk to many AI models and organize AI helpers into teams.
useFor: Chat with several AI models from one page
Group AI agents into a team that shares context
Run an AI agent on a schedule
steps: Install Docker on the machine that will host it.
In a terminal, run the setup script from the README, then `docker compose up -d`.
Open it in your browser, add your model providers and create agents.
Check the LobeHub Community License before any commercial use.

github/spec-kit.what: An open-source toolkit that provides structured templates, workflows, and agent slash commands to guide AI coding assistants through software development and bug fixing.
github/spec-kit.why: AI agents often generate code without proper planning, leading to architectural mess and skipped testing. Reach for this when you want to force your AI assistant to follow systematic steps for specifications, technical planning, and verification.
github/spec-kit.start: uv tool install specify-cli && specify init my-project --integration copilot
github/spec-kit.caution: It requires Python 3.11+, the uv installer, and a supported external AI coding agent (like GitHub Copilot) to actually interpret and run the slash commands.
github/spec-kit.plain: A GitHub toolkit that gives AI coding helpers step-by-step templates for planning and building software.
useFor: Write a clear spec before the AI starts coding
Turn a spec into a task list the AI works through
Guide GitHub Copilot through fixing a bug
steps: Install Python 3.11 or newer, the uv installer and a supported AI coding agent.
In a terminal, run `uv tool install specify-cli`.
Create a project with specify init, naming your AI agent, as the README shows.
Use the new slash commands inside your AI agent to spec, plan and build.

smtg-ai/claude-squad.what: Claude Squad is a terminal application that lets you manage and run multiple AI coding agents simultaneously in isolated environments.
smtg-ai/claude-squad.why: It prevents conflicts when running multiple AI tasks at once by orchestrating agents inside separate tmux sessions and isolated git worktrees. Use it when you need to run parallel background coding tasks with tools like Claude Code or Aider.
smtg-ai/claude-squad.caution: Requires external system dependencies including tmux and the GitHub CLI (gh) to function, and is distributed under the AGPL-3.0 license.
smtg-ai/claude-squad.plain: A terminal app for running several AI coding helpers side by side on separate tasks.
useFor: Run Claude Code and Codex on two tasks at once
Keep each agent's changes in its own workspace
Switch between running agents from one screen
steps: Install tmux and the GitHub CLI, which Claude Squad needs.
With Homebrew on Mac or Linux, in a terminal run `brew install claude-squad`.
Start it from the terminal (it installs as cs) and add a session for each task.

winfunc/opcode.what: A Tauri-based desktop interface for Claude Code that manages projects, session history, custom agents, and MCP servers.
winfunc/opcode.why: It replaces terminal-only session juggling with a visual dashboard for checkpoints, token usage tracking, and CLAUDE.md management. Reach for it when you want visual navigation and session branching over Claude Code CLI.
winfunc/opcode.start: git clone https://github.com/getAsterisk/opcode.git && cd opcode && bun install && bun run tauri dev
winfunc/opcode.caution: Prebuilt binary releases are not yet provided, so running the app requires compiling from source with Rust, Bun, and platform-specific C/system dependencies. AGPL-3.0 licensed.
winfunc/opcode.plain: A desktop app that gives Claude Code a point-and-click window for projects, sessions and agents.
useFor: Browse past Claude Code sessions in a window
Create and manage custom Claude Code agents
Manage connections to other apps without editing files
steps: Install Claude Code first, since opcode is a window on top of it.
Install Rust, Bun, Git and your system's build tools, as the README lists.
Download the code with git, then in its folder run `bun install` and the README's build command.
Expect to build it yourself, since ready-made downloads are not available yet.

siteboon/claudecodeui.what: CloudCLI is an open-source web and mobile user interface for interacting with and managing Claude Code, Cursor CLI, and Codex sessions.
siteboon/claudecodeui.why: It provides a graphical interface with integrated file navigation, Git controls, and terminal access to manage coding agent sessions locally or remotely without being tied to a command-line interface.
siteboon/claudecodeui.caution: Self-hosting exposes terminal and file system controls over a network port; requires Node.js v22 or higher, and agent execution tools are disabled by default to prevent unintended actions.
siteboon/claudecodeui.plain: A web and phone app that lets you control Claude Code and similar coding helpers from a browser.
useFor: Check on a running Claude Code session from your phone
Browse project files and changes without a terminal
Start new coding chats from a browser tab
steps: Install Node.js version 22 or newer, plus Claude Code, Cursor CLI, or Codex.
In a terminal, run `npx @cloudcli-ai/cloudcli` to start the app.
Open the local address it shows in your browser and pick a project.
Or skip installing and try the hosted CloudCLI Cloud version from the project page.

bmad-code-org/BMAD-METHOD.what: Turn ideas into working software using AI-driven development workflows, explicit planning, and structured context.
bmad-code-org/BMAD-METHOD.why: It solves the problem of coding assistants making unstated assumptions by keeping decisions explicit and carrying context forward across tasks. Reach for it when you want structured agile workflows and specialized agent perspectives inside your coding assistant.
bmad-code-org/BMAD-METHOD.plain: A set of add-ons that makes your AI coding helper plan like a product team before it builds.
useFor: Turn a rough app idea into a written plan and tasks
Get product, design, and testing viewpoints on a feature
Keep an AI coding helper on track across many sessions
steps: Have an AI coding tool installed, such as Claude Code or Cursor.
In a terminal inside your project folder, run `npx skills add bmad-code-org/BMAD-METHOD`.
When asked, pick your coding tool and the skills you want, including bmad for setup and help.
In your coding tool, ask for bmad status to see what to run next.

coleam00/Archon.what: Archon is an open-source harness builder for AI coding agents that lets you define development processes as YAML workflows for deterministic and repeatable execution.
coleam00/Archon.why: It solves the unpredictability of AI coding assistants by chaining together planning, execution, testing, and review steps into reliable, isolated pipelines. Reach for it when you want to turn ad-hoc AI interactions into structured software engineering workflows.
coleam00/Archon.start:
git clone https://github.com/coleam00/Archon
cd Archon
bun install
claude
coleam00/Archon.caution: Requires external dependencies like Bun, Claude Code, and the GitHub CLI to function properly.
coleam00/Archon.plain: Turns your AI coding helper's work into fixed checklists, so every task follows the same reliable steps.
useFor: Run the same plan, build, test, review routine on every task
Hand a GitHub issue number to AI and get a fix
Make AI coding results repeatable instead of hit-or-miss
steps: Install Claude Code, Bun, and the GitHub CLI first, as the README lists.
In a terminal, run `curl -fsSL https://archon.diy/install | bash` (Windows uses the PowerShell line in the README).
Open your project folder in a terminal, start Claude Code, and say Set up Archon.
Then ask things like Use archon to fix issue #42.

Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-claudecode.what: Teams-first multi-agent orchestration and automation plugin for Claude Code.
Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-claudecode.why: It orchestrates multiple sub-agents and automated workflows directly within Claude Code to handle complex, multi-step engineering tasks.
Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-claudecode.caution: Named autopilot stage profiles currently require Linux with the flock utility.
Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-claudecode.plain: An add-on that lets Claude Code split a big job across a team of AI helpers.
useFor: Describe an app and let several AI helpers build it
Run a hands-off plan, build, and check cycle
Speed up large coding tasks by working in parallel
steps: Open Claude Code and add the marketplace with /plugin marketplace add and this repo's GitHub link.
Inside Claude Code, run `/plugin install oh-my-claudecode`, then run /omc-setup.
Give it a task with /autopilot followed by what you want built, in quotes.

thedotmack/claude-mem.what: Captures session activity from coding agents, compresses it using AI, and injects relevant context back into future sessions.
thedotmack/claude-mem.why: Coding agents frequently forget project history when sessions restart; this tool maintains continuity of knowledge so you do not have to re-explain context.
thedotmack/claude-mem.caution: The project claims automatic off-plan observation and free trial periods that automatically fall back to your Anthropic plan, which may have privacy or cost implications depending on your setup.
thedotmack/claude-mem.plain: Gives Claude Code a memory, so it remembers what you worked on in earlier sessions.
useFor: Pick up yesterday's project without re-explaining everything
Look back at what the AI did in past sessions
Stop repeating the same project background every time
steps: Make sure Claude Code is installed and working.
In a terminal, run `npx claude-mem install`.
Restart Claude Code; notes from past sessions now appear in new ones automatically.
Check its privacy and cost notes first, since it uses AI to summarize your sessions.

EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin.what: A plugin providing 36 skills for AI coding agents to structure workflows around a brainstorm-plan-build-review-compound loop.
EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin.why: It prevents technical debt by capturing learnings from each engineering task so future changes start with better context and built-in rules.
EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin.plain: An add-on of 36 ready-made skills that teaches your AI coding helper to brainstorm, plan, build, and review.
useFor: Brainstorm and plan a feature before any code is written
Get an AI review of changes before you keep them
Save lessons from each task so the next goes smoother
steps: Open Claude Code and run /plugin marketplace add EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin.
Inside Claude Code, run `/plugin install compound-engineering`.
Cursor and Codex users can install it from their own plugin marketplace instead.

anthropics/claude-code-action.what: A general-purpose Claude Code GitHub action that answers questions, reviews code, and implements changes in PRs and issues.
anthropics/claude-code-action.why: Automates code reviews, issue triage, and code implementation directly inside GitHub workflows. Reach for it when you want Claude to interact with your pull requests and repository events automatically.
anthropics/claude-code-action.caution: Requires repository admin access to install the GitHub app and configure secrets.
anthropics/claude-code-action.plain: Lets Claude answer questions, review changes, and make fixes right inside your GitHub projects.
useFor: Get an automatic review on every proposed code change
Ask Claude to fix a bug straight from a GitHub issue
Answer teammates' questions about the code in GitHub comments
steps: You need admin access to the GitHub repository and a Claude Code install.
In a terminal inside the project, start Claude Code by typing claude.
Inside Claude Code, run `/install-github-app` and follow the guided setup for the app and secrets.
Then mention Claude in an issue or pull request comment to give it a task.

songquanpeng/one-api.what: An LLM API management and key redistribution system that unifies multiple AI providers under a single OpenAI-compatible API.
songquanpeng/one-api.why: To manage multiple large language model providers, handle load balancing, set up user billing or token quotas, and distribute API keys through a single interface.
songquanpeng/one-api.start: docker run --name one-api -d --restart always -p 3000:3000 -e TZ=Asia/Shanghai -v /home/ubuntu/data/one-api:/data justsong/one-api
songquanpeng/one-api.caution: Must change the default root password (123456) immediately upon first login.
songquanpeng/one-api.plain: A self-hosted hub that puts many AI services behind one key, so you can manage and share access.
useFor: Give a team one AI key instead of many accounts
Switch between AI providers without changing your apps
Track and limit how much each person uses
steps: Install Docker on a computer or server that stays on.
In a terminal, start it with the docker run command from the README.
Open port 3000 in your browser and log in as root.
Change the default password 123456 right away, then add your AI provider keys.

QuantumNous/new-api.what: A self-hosted AI gateway that aggregates and distributes various LLM services under unified API formats.
QuantumNous/new-api.why: It solves the problem of managing multiple upstream LLM providers and disparate API keys by centralizing routing, access control, usage analytics, and cost accounting. Reach for it when you want to run a private multi-model service or share authorized model access across a team.
QuantumNous/new-api.plain: A self-hosted hub that combines many AI services into one address and one set of keys.
useFor: Route all your AI tools through one shared key
Mix cheaper and premium AI models behind one address
Share AI access with a team and see usage
steps: Install Docker on the computer or server that will host it.
In a terminal, run the docker run command from the README to start it.
Open localhost port 3000 in your browser to set it up and add provider keys.

router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI.what: CLIProxyAPI provides OpenAI, Gemini, Claude, Codex, and Grok compatible API interfaces for CLI and desktop clients.
router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI.why: It bridges multiple CLI accounts and proprietary provider interfaces into standard OpenAI/Gemini/Claude-compatible endpoints so you can access them from any client or SDK.
