router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI.caution: It works by signing in with your CLI or subscription accounts (OAuth) and re-exposing them as an API. Check each provider's terms first: using a consumer subscription as a general-purpose API may not be allowed and can get the account limited. The README also contains affiliate links.
router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI.plain: Turns your existing AI subscriptions into a standard connection other apps can use.
useFor: Use your Claude or ChatGPT plan inside other coding tools
Point several AI apps at one local connection
Switch between AI accounts from a single place
steps: Read each provider's terms first; using a consumer plan this way may not be allowed.
Follow the install guide on the CLIProxyAPI help site linked in the README.
Sign in with your AI accounts, then point your apps at the address it provides.
Prefer a desktop helper? The README lists community tray and dashboard apps that manage it.

rtk-ai/rtk.what: High-performance CLI proxy that intercepts and compresses shell command outputs before they reach your coding agent's context window.
rtk-ai/rtk.why: Coding agents often spew thousands of lines of raw terminal output from commands like git status, test suites, and file reads into the LLM context. Reach for RTK to dramatically slash bash output volume, reduce token waste, and speed up agent workflows.
rtk-ai/rtk.caution: The repository claims up to 90% bash output reduction, but this refers strictly to shell output size, not your total API bill. Token counts are approximated using bytes/4 rather than a precise tokenizer.
rtk-ai/rtk.plain: A small helper that trims long terminal output before your AI coding tool reads it, saving tokens.
useFor: Cut the text your AI agent reads from test runs
Stretch your AI coding plan's limits further
Keep long command output from crowding the AI's memory
steps: Install it with Homebrew on Mac, winget on Windows, or the install script in the README.
In a terminal, run `rtk init -g` to hook it into your AI coding tool.
Keep working as usual; savings apply to command output, not your whole AI bill.

microsoft/LLMLingua.what: It compresses prompts and KV-caches using smaller companion models to reduce token counts and lower API costs.
microsoft/LLMLingua.why: It solves the problem of high API costs and context window limits when sending massive prompts to large language models. Reach for it when you want to squeeze longer documents or RAG contexts into fewer tokens without retraining your main model.
microsoft/LLMLingua.plain: A code library that shortens the text you send to AI, cutting cost while keeping the meaning.
useFor: Shrink long documents before sending them to a paid AI model
Fit more background text into one AI request
Lower the monthly bill of an AI feature you run
steps: Have Python installed on your computer.
In a terminal, run `pip install llmlingua`.
Add it to your Python code using the examples in the README to compress prompts.

Maciek-roboblog/Claude-Code-Usage-Monito.what: Real-time Claude Code usage monitor with predictions and warnings.
Maciek-roboblog/Claude-Code-Usage-Monito.why: It tracks token consumption, message counts, and costs for Claude Code sessions to prevent hitting limits unexpectedly. Reach for it when you need visibility into your active agent token usage and spend.
Maciek-roboblog/Claude-Code-Usage-Monito.plain: A live terminal display showing how much of your Claude Code limit you have used and when it runs out.
useFor: See how close you are to your Claude Code limit
Get a warning before you run out mid-task
Plan heavy work around when your limit resets
steps: Install the uv tool for Python if you do not have it.
In a terminal, run `uv tool install claude-monitor`.
Type claude-monitor in a terminal and leave it open while you work.

Kilo-Org/kilocode.what: Kilo Code is an AI coding agent available in VS Code, JetBrains, and the command line that lets you build and edit code using over 500 different models.
Kilo-Org/kilocode.why: Use this when you want an open source coding assistant that integrates directly into your editor or terminal and lets you switch between different AI models without paying a markup.
Kilo-Org/kilocode.caution: Autonomous mode (--auto) auto-approves permission prompts and should only be used in trusted environments.
Kilo-Org/kilocode.plain: An open source AI coding helper for VS Code, JetBrains, or the terminal that works with hundreds of models.
useFor: Ask AI to build or change code inside your editor
Try different AI models and pick the cheapest that works
Fix errors in a project by describing the problem
steps: Install the Kilo Code extension from the VS Code Marketplace, or use the JetBrains version.
Create an account or add your own AI provider key when it asks.
For the terminal version, run `npm install -g @kilocode/cli` in a terminal.
Avoid auto-approve mode unless you trust the project, since it skips permission prompts.

zed-industries/zed.what: Zed is a high-performance, multiplayer code editor from the creators of Atom and Tree-sitter.
zed-industries/zed.why: Use it when you want a fast, collaborative code editor built for modern development workflows.
zed-industries/zed.start: Download Zed directly from zed.dev/download or install it via your local package manager on macOS, Linux, or Windows.
zed-industries/zed.caution: Source code is licensed primarily under GPL-3.0-or-later with Apache-2.0 components.
zed-industries/zed.plain: A fast code editor with built-in AI help and live editing with teammates.
useFor: Write and edit code with an AI helper beside it
Edit the same file live with a teammate
Open big projects quickly on an older laptop
steps: Download Zed from zed.dev/download for Mac, Windows, or Linux.
Install it and open a project folder.
Connect an AI model in its settings to use the AI assistant.

charmbracelet/crush.what: Crush is an agentic coding assistant that runs in your terminal, connecting your tools, code, and workflows to multiple LLM providers.
charmbracelet/crush.why: It is used when you want a terminal-based coding partner that supports multiple models with mid-session switching, LSP integration, and MCP capabilities.
charmbracelet/crush.caution: The repository licence is marked as NOASSERTION.
charmbracelet/crush.plain: A friendly AI coding helper that runs in your terminal and works with many AI providers.
useFor: Ask AI to explain or change code in a project folder
Switch between AI providers without changing tools
Run coding tasks from the terminal instead of an editor
steps: In a terminal, install it with `brew install charmbracelet/tap/crush` (npm and other options are in the README).
Get an API key from an AI provider you want to use.
Open your project folder in a terminal and type crush to start.

QwenLM/qwen-code.what: An open-source AI coding agent that lives in your terminal, editor, desktop, browser, and chat apps.
QwenLM/qwen-code.why: It handles complex multi-step coding tasks, repository searches, and terminal workflows. Reach for it when you want an open-source alternative to proprietary coding agents.
QwenLM/qwen-code.caution: Integrates across multiple desktop, terminal, and web interfaces with various third-party APIs and local models, which may introduce configuration complexity or security considerations.
QwenLM/qwen-code.plain: An open AI coding helper from the Qwen team that works in your terminal, editor, and chat apps.
useFor: Ask AI to write or fix code in a project
Use Qwen or local models instead of paid services
Get coding help across terminal, editor, and chat
steps: In a terminal, run the one-line install script from the README.
Go to your project folder in the terminal and type qwen to start.
Follow the prompts to connect a model or API key.

plandex-ai/plandex.what: Plandex is a terminal-based AI coding agent designed to handle large multi-file tasks and complex codebases.
plandex-ai/plandex.why: Use this when other AI coding tools struggle with the size or complexity of a large codebase, as it features a sandbox for reviewing edits and a 2M token effective context window.
plandex-ai/plandex.caution: Plandex Cloud is winding down as of October 2025; users must rely on self-hosted or local mode with their own API keys or supported subscriptions.
plandex-ai/plandex.plain: A terminal AI coding helper built for big changes that touch many files at once.
useFor: Plan and carry out a change across dozens of files
Review AI changes safely before they touch your project
Work on very large codebases other tools struggle with
steps: The hosted Plandex Cloud is shutting down, so plan to use local mode with your own API keys.
In a terminal, run `curl -sL https://plandex.ai/install.sh | bash`.
Follow the local mode quickstart in its docs to connect your models.

openinterpreter/openinterpreter.what: A coding agent optimized for low-cost models with built-in harness emulation and a terminal interface.
openinterpreter/openinterpreter.why: It allows developers to run coding agents using lower-cost or open-weight models while retaining compatibility with multiple agent harnesses and protocols like ACP and Codex.
openinterpreter/openinterpreter.plain: A terminal AI coding helper tuned to work well with cheaper AI models.
useFor: Get coding help while paying less for the AI model
Ask AI to run and fix code in your terminal
Try budget models on real coding tasks
steps: In a terminal on Mac or Linux, run `curl -fsSL https://www.openinterpreter.com/install | sh`.
On Windows, use the PowerShell install line from the README instead.
Type i or interpreter in a terminal to start a session.

Significant-Gravitas/AutoGPT.what: AutoGPT lets you build, deploy, and run autonomous AI agents that carry out complete workflows via a visual builder or plain English.
Significant-Gravitas/AutoGPT.why: It solves the problem of manual multi-step task execution, allowing you to automate repetitive chores by leveraging AI agents. Reach for it when you want to build or run automated workflows connected to hundreds of apps and AI models.
Significant-Gravitas/AutoGPT.caution: Self-hosting requires Docker, configuration, and your own model API keys, while the hosted platform is a paid service.
Significant-Gravitas/AutoGPT.plain: A platform where you build AI helpers that carry out whole tasks on their own, using a visual editor.
useFor: Build an AI helper that drafts social posts from your content
Automate a multi-step research and writing routine
Create a workflow by describing it in plain English
steps: Sign up for the hosted AutoGPT Platform from the Get started link in the README.
Describe what you want or drag blocks together in the visual builder.
To self-host instead, follow the getting started docs; this needs Docker and your own AI keys.

microsoft/agent-framework.what: Microsoft Agent Framework is a multi-language library for building, orchestrating, and deploying production-grade AI agents and multi-agent workflows in Python, .NET, and Go.
microsoft/agent-framework.why: It helps teams move from prototype to production by providing graph-based workflows, durability, human-in-the-loop controls, and OpenTelemetry observability. Reach for it when building complex multi-agent systems that require enterprise governance.
microsoft/agent-framework.plain: Microsoft's code toolkit for building AI helpers and teams of helpers in Python, .NET, or Go.
useFor: Build an AI assistant into your company's software
Coordinate several AI helpers that pass work along
Move a prototype AI agent into production use
steps: Have Python, .NET, or Go set up on your computer.
For Python, run `pip install agent-framework` in a terminal.
Follow the getting started samples in the repo to write your first agent.

pydantic/pydantic-ai.what: Pydantic AI is a Python framework for building typed, extensible AI agents with model swapping and built-in capabilities like memory and guardrails.
pydantic/pydantic-ai.why: Use this when you want to build robust AI agents, data extraction pipelines, or durable workflows in Python with end-to-end type safety.
pydantic/pydantic-ai.caution: Complex ecosystem with multiple separate packages for graphs, evals, and observability.
pydantic/pydantic-ai.plain: A Python code toolkit for building reliable AI helpers that can switch between AI models easily.
useFor: Build an AI helper that returns clean, structured answers
Swap AI providers without rewriting your app
Add memory and safety checks to an AI feature
steps: Have Python and the uv tool installed.
In a terminal inside your project, run `uv add pydantic-ai pydantic-ai-harness`.
Write a small agent using the examples in the README and docs.

huggingface/smolagents.what: A minimalist library for building code-writing agents with minimal abstractions.
huggingface/smolagents.why: Use this when you want to build custom agents that execute actions by writing Python code rather than structured JSON outputs, keeping your agent logic transparent and easy to debug.
huggingface/smolagents.caution: Executing model-generated code can be dangerous unless run inside a sandboxed environment.
huggingface/smolagents.plain: A small Python code library for building AI helpers that solve tasks by writing and running code.
useFor: Build an AI helper that searches the web and summarizes
Let AI crunch numbers by writing its own small programs
Experiment with AI agents using very little code
steps: Have Python installed on your computer.
In a terminal, run `pip install "smolagents[toolkit]"`.
Follow the README example, and run generated code in a sandbox to stay safe.

agno-agi/agno.what: Agno is a framework and runtime for building, running, and managing custom AI agent platforms.
agno-agi/agno.why: It provides developers with a complete stack to build agent applications, serve them via APIs, handle storage, and manage platforms with built-in observability, security, and multi-tenant isolation.
agno-agi/agno.start: Clone https://github.com/agno-agi/agentos-railway into a folder called agent-platform, cd in, read the README, and follow the get started guide.
agno-agi/agno.caution: Sends telemetry data per agent run by default, which can be disabled via an environment variable.
agno-agi/agno.plain: A code toolkit and runtime for building and running your own AI helpers and managing them in one place.
useFor: Build a set of company AI helpers you host yourself
Run and monitor several AI agents from one dashboard
Turn an AI agent prototype into a running service
steps: Download the agentos-railway starter from GitHub into a folder named agent-platform.
Read that folder's README and follow its get started guide.
It sends usage data per run by default; turn it off with the setting its docs describe.

mastra-ai/mastra.what: Mastra is a TypeScript framework for building AI applications, autonomous agents, and multi-step workflows.
mastra-ai/mastra.why: It provides a structured way to handle model routing, graph-based workflows, human-in-the-loop state suspension, and evaluation for web developers building production AI features.
mastra-ai/mastra.caution: Dual-licensed with an enterprise license on specific enterprise directories.
mastra-ai/mastra.plain: A TypeScript code toolkit for building AI apps, helpers, and multi-step AI workflows.
useFor: Add an AI assistant to a web app you are building
Build a multi-step AI workflow like research then report
Connect AI helpers to your company's tools and data
steps: Have Node.js installed on your computer.
In a terminal, run `npm create mastra@latest` and answer the setup questions.
Open the new project and follow its docs to build your first agent.

google/adk-python.what: An open-source, code-first Python framework for building, evaluating, and deploying AI agents and multi-agent systems.
google/adk-python.why: It provides a graph-based workflow runtime, task delegation APIs, and deployment tools so developers can build structured, production-ready AI applications. Reach for it when you need to orchestrate complex agent behaviors beyond simple chat loops.
google/adk-python.plain: Google's Python code toolkit for building, testing, and launching AI helpers and teams of helpers.
useFor: Build an AI helper that uses your own tools
Test how well an AI agent handles sample tasks
Deploy an AI agent to Google Cloud
steps: Have Python installed on your computer.
In a terminal, run `pip install google-adk`.
Follow the quickstart in the ADK docs to build and try your first agent.

modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk.what: Official TypeScript SDK for building Model Context Protocol servers and clients across Node.js, Bun, and Deno.
modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk.why: Provides standardized tools and resources to connect AI models with external data sources and applications. Reach for it when building custom MCP servers or clients in TypeScript.
modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk.plain: The official TypeScript code kit for making connectors that let AI assistants use your apps and data.
useFor: Build a connector so Claude can read your company database
Give AI assistants access to an internal tool
Make your product usable from AI chat apps
steps: Have Node.js, Bun, or Deno set up.
In a terminal inside your project, run `npm install @modelcontextprotocol/server`.
Follow the README examples to build a server, then add it to your AI app.

modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk.what: The official Python SDK for building Model Context Protocol servers and clients.
modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk.why: It allows developers to expose data and functionality to LLM applications in a standardized way using Python type hints, without writing manual JSON schemas or request parsing.
modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk.caution: Requires Python 3.10+ and uses v2 of the SDK, which includes breaking changes from v1.
modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk.plain: The official Python code kit for making connectors that let AI assistants use your apps and data.
useFor: Build a connector so Claude can search your files
Let an AI assistant call your own Python scripts
Share a company tool with AI chat apps
steps: Have Python 3.10 or newer and the uv tool installed.
In a terminal inside your project, run `uv add "mcp[cli]"`.
Follow the README examples to write a server; note v2 differs from older v1 guides.

PrefectHQ/fastmcp.what: FastMCP is a framework for building Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, clients, and interactive apps in Python and TypeScript.
PrefectHQ/fastmcp.why: Building MCP servers manually requires handling protocol lifecycles, schema validation, and transport negotiation, which FastMCP automates so you can turn ordinary functions into LLM tools instantly.
PrefectHQ/fastmcp.plain: A popular Python code toolkit that makes building connectors between AI assistants and your tools quick.
useFor: Turn a Python script into a tool Claude can use
Connect an AI assistant to an internal service
Build a small app that shows up inside AI chats
steps: Have Python and the uv tool installed.
In a terminal inside your project, run `uv add fastmcp`.
Follow the README quickstart to write your first server and connect it to your AI app.

browserbase/stagehand.what: Stagehand is an SDK for browser agents that extracts data and interacts with websites using natural language commands.
browserbase/stagehand.why: Use it when building web automation or scraping agents that need to self-heal when site layouts change and extract structured schema-validated data.
browserbase/stagehand.caution: Requires a local installation of Google Chrome and a valid LLM API key to process instructions.
browserbase/stagehand.plain: A code toolkit that lets programs use websites by giving plain-English instructions like click the login button.
useFor: Collect prices from several shopping sites automatically
Automate filling the same web form every week
Build an AI helper that browses and reports back
steps: Install Google Chrome and get an API key from an AI provider.
In a terminal inside a JavaScript project, run `pnpm add @browserbasehq/stagehand 'zod@~4.4.3'`.
Write a short script using the README examples to open a page and act on it.

Skyvern-AI/skyvern.what: Automates browser-based workflows using Vision LLMs and Playwright.
Skyvern-AI/skyvern.why: Traditional browser automation scripts break when website layouts change. Skyvern uses computer vision and LLMs to interact with websites reliably without relying on brittle XPaths or DOM selectors.
Skyvern-AI/skyvern.caution: Requires external LLM API keys and relies on computer vision models, which can be computationally intensive or prone to occasional visual misinterpretation.
Skyvern-AI/skyvern.plain: An AI helper that looks at websites like a person and carries out web tasks for you.
useFor: Fill out the same online form across many sites
Download invoices from websites without clicking through each one
Automate a repetitive routine in a web portal
steps: Get an API key from an AI provider, or use the hosted Skyvern Cloud instead.
In a terminal, run `pip install "skyvern[all]" && skyvern quickstart`.
Follow the quickstart prompts, then describe the web task you want done.

exo-explore/exo.what: Connects all your devices into an AI cluster to run models larger than would fit on a single device.
exo-explore/exo.why: It lets you distribute large AI models across multiple computers and use device-to-device communication to speed up inference.
exo-explore/exo.caution: Linux support currently runs on CPU and GPU support is under active development.
exo-explore/exo.plain: Links your computers together so they can run a big AI model none could handle alone.
useFor: Run a large AI model at home across two Macs
Chat with a private AI without sending data online
Reuse spare computers instead of paying for cloud AI
steps: On a Mac with macOS Tahoe 26.2 or later, download the EXO app from the README link.
Otherwise install uv, Node.js, and Rust, then download the code and build the dashboard as the README shows.
In a terminal in the exo folder, run `uv run exo` on each device.
Open the built-in dashboard to manage the cluster and chat with models.

sgl-project/sglang.what: SGLang is a high-performance serving framework for large language models and multimodal models designed to deliver low-latency and high-throughput inference.
sgl-project/sglang.why: It solves the bottleneck of slow and expensive model inference by providing advanced features like RadixAttention prefix caching and prefill-decode disaggregation, making it ideal when you need to serve open-weight models at scale.
sgl-project/sglang.caution: Requires dedicated GPU hardware (such as NVIDIA or AMD accelerators) and advanced configuration for distributed clusters.
sgl-project/sglang.plain: Server software that runs AI models fast for many users at once on your own graphics cards.
useFor: Host an open AI model for your whole team
Serve AI answers faster and cheaper on your own hardware
Power a company chatbot without a cloud AI provider
steps: You need a machine with a strong NVIDIA or AMD graphics card.
In a terminal, run `pip install sglang`.
Follow the docs to launch a model server and connect your apps to it.

janhq/jan.what: Jan is an open-source ChatGPT alternative that runs large language models locally and completely offline on your computer.
janhq/jan.why: It keeps your conversations completely private and under your control without requiring an internet connection or external cloud API. Reach for it when you want to run open-weight models on your own desktop hardware.
janhq/jan.start: git clone https://github.com/janhq/jan && cd jan && make dev
janhq/jan.plain: A free ChatGPT-style app that runs AI on your own computer, fully offline if you want.
useFor: Chat with AI on a plane or without internet
Ask about private documents without sending them online
Try free open AI models before paying for one
steps: Download Jan for Windows, Mac, or Linux from jan.ai or the GitHub releases page.
Install and open it, then download a model from inside the app.
Start chatting; optionally add cloud AI keys for models like Claude.

nomic-ai/gpt4all.what: GPT4All runs large language models privately on everyday desktops and laptops without requiring API calls or specialized GPUs.
nomic-ai/gpt4all.why: It lets you run open-source AI models completely offline for local chat and data privacy, and you should reach for it when you want to experiment with or use LLMs locally.
nomic-ai/gpt4all.plain: A free app that runs AI chatbots privately on an ordinary laptop, no internet or special hardware needed.
useFor: Chat with AI without sending anything to the internet
Ask questions about your local documents
Use AI on a laptop without a gaming graphics card
steps: Download the installer for Windows, Mac, or Ubuntu from the README.
Install and open it, then pick a model to download.
Start chatting, or add a folder of documents to ask about.

ml-explore/mlx-lm.what: MLX LM is a Python package for generating text, fine-tuning, and quantizing large language models specifically on Apple Silicon using the MLX framework.
ml-explore/mlx-lm.why: It enables running and fine-tuning open-weight models locally on Mac hardware with native optimization. Reach for this when you want to run LLMs privately on Apple Silicon without third-party API dependencies.
ml-explore/mlx-lm.caution: Requires an Apple Silicon Mac, and certain large models or features require macOS 15.0 or higher.
ml-explore/mlx-lm.plain: A tool that runs and fine-tunes AI text models fast on Apple Silicon Macs.
useFor: Run an open AI model privately on your MacBook
Teach a small model your own writing style
Shrink a model so it fits in your Mac's memory
steps: You need a Mac with an Apple Silicon chip; some features need macOS 15 or later.
In a terminal, run `pip install mlx-lm`.
Use its generate and chat commands from the README to try a model.

LostRuins/koboldcpp.what: KoboldCpp is an easy-to-use AI text-generation software for GGML and GGUF models that features a built-in KoboldAI Lite UI and supports multiple local modalities.
LostRuins/koboldcpp.why: It provides a self-contained executable to run open-weight AI models locally on your CPU or GPU without complex installations. Reach for it when you want a feature-rich, all-in-one local runner with built-in chat, adventure, and storywriting modes.
LostRuins/koboldcpp.caution: There are active phishing sites impersonating the download page; ensure you only download binaries from the official GitHub repository releases.
LostRuins/koboldcpp.plain: A single download that runs AI text models on your computer with a built-in chat screen.
useFor: Write stories with an AI on your own computer
Chat with a private AI model without installing extras
Try open models on an older PC
steps: Download only from the official GitHub releases page; fake lookalike sites exist.
On Windows, run koboldcpp.exe; on Mac or Linux, download the matching file and run it.
Load a GGUF model file in the settings window, then chat in the browser page.

chroma-core/chroma.what: Chroma is an open-source vector database that stores and searches embeddings for AI applications.
chroma-core/chroma.why: It provides a simple way to store documents, metadata, and vector embeddings so an AI can search through private data or context. Reach for it when building retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) applications that require similarity search.
chroma-core/chroma.plain: A database that stores text by meaning so AI apps can find related information quickly.
useFor: Build a chatbot that answers from your company documents
Find similar support tickets by meaning, not keywords
Give an AI app long-term memory
steps: Have Python installed on your computer.
In a terminal, run `pip install chromadb`.
Follow the README example to add documents and search them in code.

qdrant/qdrant.what: High-performance vector search engine and database written in Rust for storing embeddings and filtering payloads.
qdrant/qdrant.why: Use this when you need to build semantic search engines, recommendation systems, or Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) applications that require fast, scalable vector similarity matching with complex payload filtering.
qdrant/qdrant.caution: Running the default Docker container starts an insecure deployment without authentication; secure your instance before production use.
qdrant/qdrant.plain: A fast database for finding information by meaning, used behind AI search and chatbots.
useFor: Power search that finds answers by meaning in your documents
Recommend similar products or articles
Store memory for an AI assistant at large scale
steps: Install Docker, or use the managed Qdrant Cloud, which has a free tier.
In a terminal, run `docker run -p 6333:6333 qdrant/qdrant`.
Connect from your code using the README examples; add security before real use.

HKUDS/LightRAG.what: LightRAG is a simple and fast retrieval-augmented generation framework that uses dual-level retrieval and knowledge graphs to answer questions from your documents.
HKUDS/LightRAG.why: Traditional RAG struggles with complex queries that require connecting multiple pieces of information across large text corpora. Reach for LightRAG when you need an efficient, graph-based RAG system that supports multimodal data parsing, multiple storage backends, and role-specific LLM configurations.
HKUDS/LightRAG.caution: The project integrates many external services like MinerU, Docling, and various vector and graph databases, which can add complexity to your setup.
HKUDS/LightRAG.plain: A code toolkit that lets AI answer questions about your documents by mapping how their ideas connect.
useFor: Ask questions across a big pile of reports
Build a Q&A assistant for company manuals
See how people, places, and topics in documents connect
steps: Have Python installed and an AI provider key ready.
In a terminal, run `pip install lightrag-hku`.
Follow the README examples to load documents and ask questions.

microsoft/graphrag.what: A data pipeline and transformation suite designed to extract structured data from unstructured text using LLMs to build knowledge graphs for question answering.
microsoft/graphrag.why: It improves LLM reasoning over private datasets by organizing text into structured knowledge graphs. Reach for it when standard vector search RAG struggles to connect disparate facts across large corpora.
microsoft/graphrag.caution: The project is largely in maintenance mode. Indexing can be an expensive operation with high LLM token costs, so start small and read the cost documentation carefully.
microsoft/graphrag.plain: Microsoft's tool that turns piles of text into a map of connected facts AI can answer questions from.
useFor: Answer big-picture questions across hundreds of documents
Pull out people, companies, and links from reports
Summarize themes across a large text collection
steps: Prefer an alternative: LightRAG, since GraphRAG is largely in maintenance mode.
Read the cost docs first; indexing can use a lot of paid AI tokens.
In a terminal, set up a project with `graphrag init --root [path] --force`.
Start with a small set of documents, then follow the docs to index and ask questions.

docling-project/docling.what: Docling simplifies document processing by parsing diverse formats including advanced PDF understanding and providing integrations with the generative AI ecosystem.
docling-project/docling.why: It solves the difficulty of turning complex, multi-format documents like PDFs, DOCX, and scanned images into structured markdown, JSON, or text for AI applications. Reach for it when building RAG systems or data pipelines that need clean document ingestion.
docling-project/docling.plain: A tool that turns PDFs, Word files, and other documents into clean text AI can read.
useFor: Convert a stack of PDFs into editable text
Pull tables out of reports cleanly
Prepare documents so an AI chatbot can answer from them
steps: Have Python installed on your computer.
In a terminal, run `pip install docling`.
Then run docling followed by a file path or web link to get a Markdown file.

unclecode/crawl4ai.what: Crawl4AI turns any website into clean, LLM-ready Markdown for RAG, AI agents, and data pipelines.
unclecode/crawl4ai.why: It solves the problem of extracting clean text from messy web pages, helping developers feed up-to-date web content into language models or applications.
unclecode/crawl4ai.caution: Requires installing a headless browser environment via setup commands to handle dynamic JavaScript-heavy web pages.
unclecode/crawl4ai.plain: A free tool that turns websites into clean text ready for AI to read and use.
useFor: Save a whole documentation site as clean text
Collect articles to feed an AI chatbot
Gather web data for a research project
steps: Have Python installed on your computer.
In a terminal, run `pip install -U crawl4ai`, then crawl4ai-setup to install the browser it uses.
Run crawl4ai-doctor to check it works, then use the README examples.

firecrawl/firecrawl.what: An API and set of developer tools to search, scrape, crawl, and interact with websites at scale, turning messy HTML into clean Markdown or structured data for AI agents.
firecrawl/firecrawl.why: Web scraping is notoriously fragile due to JavaScript-heavy pages, anti-bot protections, and changing layouts; use this when you need reliable web data extracted directly into formats suitable for LLMs without maintaining custom scrapers.
firecrawl/firecrawl.start:
from firecrawl import Firecrawl

app = Firecrawl(api_key="fc-YOUR_API_KEY")

result = app.scrape('firecrawl.dev')
firecrawl/firecrawl.caution: Requires an API key from firecrawl.dev and relies on a hosted cloud service for its primary functionality.
firecrawl/firecrawl.plain: An online service that reads websites and turns them into clean text or data for AI.
useFor: Turn a list of web pages into clean text for AI
Search the web and pull structured data from results
Give an AI helper the ability to read live websites
steps: Sign up at firecrawl.dev to get an API key.
In a terminal, install the Python library with `pip install firecrawl-py`.
Follow the README example to scrape a page with your key.

letta-ai/letta.what: Letta (formerly MemGPT) is a platform for building stateful AI agents with memory that can learn and self-improve over time.
letta-ai/letta.why: It solves the problem of stateless AI by providing advanced memory systems for agents, and you should reach for it when you need agents that retain information and identity across sessions.
letta-ai/letta.caution: The current active source code has moved to a separate repository (letta-ai/letta-code).
letta-ai/letta.plain: A platform for AI helpers that remember you and get better over time.
useFor: Build an assistant that remembers past conversations
Keep one AI helper's knowledge across many sessions
Run a personal agent from the desktop app
steps: Note that active development now lives in the letta-ai/letta-code repository.
In a terminal, run `npm install -g @letta-ai/letta-code`.
Type letta to start, or use the desktop app for Mac, Windows, or Linux.

topoteretes/cognee.what: Cognee is an open-source AI memory platform that gives AI agents persistent long-term memory across sessions by turning documents, code, and conversations into a knowledge graph.
topoteretes/cognee.why: It solves the problem of agents forgetting context between runs and helps developers build a shared knowledge base or company brain that agents can search and reuse.
topoteretes/cognee.caution: The bundled GLiNER extractor is a demo of the small-model pipeline; production-ready accuracy may require external LLM setup.
topoteretes/cognee.plain: Gives AI helpers a lasting memory by turning your documents and chats into a map of connected facts.
useFor: Let an AI helper remember facts across sessions
Ask questions over your documents and past chats
Connect notes, code, and conversations into one memory
steps: Have Python and the uv tool installed.
In a terminal, run `uv pip install "cognee[gliner]"`.
Try cognee-cli remember and cognee-cli recall; add an AI model for better answers.

LibreChat-AI/LibreChat.what: An open-source ChatGPT clone with multi-user authentication, agent support, sandboxed code execution, and compatibility with dozens of AI providers.
LibreChat-AI/LibreChat.why: Provides a self-hostable, customizable web interface to chat with multiple AI models, manage custom agents, and run code securely in one place.
LibreChat-AI/LibreChat.caution: Requires configuration of backend services like MongoDB and various API keys to fully unlock all features.
LibreChat-AI/LibreChat.plain: A free, self-hosted ChatGPT-style app your team can share, working with dozens of AI providers.
useFor: Give a team one chat app with logins
Use Claude, GPT, and local models in one place
Build shared AI agents with tools for your team
steps: Install Docker and get API keys for the AI providers you want.
In a terminal, run `git clone https://github.com/LibreChat-AI/LibreChat.git`.
Follow the Docker quick start in the LibreChat docs to configure and launch it.

ChatGPTNextWeb/NextChat.what: A cross-platform AI chat assistant and web application supporting multiple model providers like OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, and DeepSeek.
ChatGPTNextWeb/NextChat.why: Provides a lightweight, customizable user interface that can be self-hosted or run on desktop and mobile devices for chatting with multiple AI models.
ChatGPTNextWeb/NextChat.start: Get an OpenAI API Key, then click the Deploy on Vercel button in the README to instantly spin up your own web app.
ChatGPTNextWeb/NextChat.plain: A clean chat app for using ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and others with your own keys.
useFor: Chat with several AI models in one app
Pay per use with your own key instead of subscriptions
Host a private chat page for your family or team
steps: Get an API key from an AI provider such as OpenAI.
Download the desktop app from the releases page, or try the web app demo.
Or click Deploy on Vercel in the README to host your own copy.

langflow-ai/langflow.what: Langflow is a visual platform for building and deploying AI-powered agents and workflows.
langflow-ai/langflow.why: It lets you design complex LLM chains and multi-agent systems visually without writing boilerplate code, and reach for it when you want a drag-and-drop builder with a Python backend.
langflow-ai/langflow.plain: A drag-and-drop builder for making AI helpers and workflows without much code.
useFor: Build a document Q&A bot by connecting blocks
Chain AI steps like summarize then email
Prototype an AI helper before handing it to developers
steps: Have Python and the uv tool installed, or use Docker.
In a terminal, run `uv pip install langflow -U`.
Start it with uv run langflow run and open the address it shows in your browser.

activepieces/activepieces.what: An open source, extensible AI workflow automation tool and Zapier alternative with TypeScript-based integration pieces that double as MCP servers.
activepieces/activepieces.why: Use this tool when you need to automate workflows and connect various APIs, databases, or AI agents using a visual builder. It helps bridge the gap between no-code automation and custom TypeScript development.
activepieces/activepieces.caution: Community Edition is MIT licensed, but enterprise features require a commercial license.
activepieces/activepieces.plain: An open Zapier-style tool for automating tasks between apps, with AI steps built in.
useFor: Save new email attachments to Google Sheets automatically
Summarize incoming messages with AI and post to Discord
Connect 200+ apps without writing code
steps: Sign up on activepieces.com, or self-host using the install guide in its docs.
Create a flow: pick a trigger app, then add action steps.
Add AI steps where needed and turn the flow on.

stackblitz-labs/bolt.diy.what: Prompt, run, edit, and deploy full-stack web applications using your choice of 19+ LLM providers.
stackblitz-labs/bolt.diy.why: It provides an open-source, customizable alternative to web-based code generators like Bolt.new, letting you swap between providers like OpenAI, Anthropic, and local models via Ollama.
stackblitz-labs/bolt.diy.plain: Describe a website or app and AI builds it, using any AI provider you choose.
useFor: Build a working website from a plain description
Make a quick prototype app to show your team
Publish a simple site to Netlify or Vercel
steps: Download the app for Windows, Mac, or Linux from the latest GitHub release.
Open it and add an API key for the AI provider you want.
Describe what you want to build, then edit, preview, and download or deploy it.

langfuse/langfuse.what: Langfuse is an open source LLM engineering platform that helps teams collaboratively trace, evaluate, prompt-manage, and debug AI applications.
langfuse/langfuse.why: It solves the problem of tracking complex LLM calls, debugging user sessions, and running evaluations without needing to build custom logging infrastructure from scratch. Reach for it when you need production observability or structured test benchmarks for your AI app.
langfuse/langfuse.plain: A dashboard for teams to see, test, and debug what their AI features are doing.
useFor: See every question and answer your AI app handled
Find which prompts give bad or costly answers
Compare prompt versions before rolling one out
steps: Use the hosted Langfuse service or self-host it with Docker.
To self-host, download the code with git clone and run `docker compose up` in a terminal in that folder.
In your Python app, install langfuse and follow the README quickstart to send traces.

promptfoo/promptfoo.what: It is a command-line tool and library for testing prompts, agents, and RAG applications, featuring automated evaluations, red teaming, and model comparison.
promptfoo/promptfoo.why: It helps developers move away from trial-and-error by providing metrics, security vulnerability scans, and CI/CD checks for LLM applications. Reach for it when you need to rigorously test output quality or pentest an AI app before shipping.
promptfoo/promptfoo.caution: The project claims evals run 100% locally, but you must still supply your own LLM API keys which send data to external providers unless using purely local models.
promptfoo/promptfoo.plain: A free tool that tests your AI prompts and chatbots automatically and flags bad or unsafe answers.
useFor: Compare answers from several AI models side by side
Check a company chatbot for unsafe or leaky replies
Catch worse answers after you change a prompt
steps: Install Node.js, then in a terminal run `npm install -g promptfoo`.
Create a starter project with promptfoo init --example getting-started.
Add your AI provider key, then run promptfoo eval and promptfoo view to see results.

Arize-ai/phoenix.what: Arize Phoenix provides OpenTelemetry-based tracing, evaluation, dataset management, and experimentation for LLM applications.
Arize-ai/phoenix.why: It solves the challenge of debugging and benchmarking complex AI workflows and multi-step agent applications. Reach for it when you need to inspect what your LLM code is doing under the hood, run evals, or manage prompts.
Arize-ai/phoenix.plain: A free dashboard that shows step by step what your AI app did and grades its answers.
useFor: See why an AI agent gave a wrong answer
Score chatbot replies against a test set
Try prompt changes and compare the results
steps: Install Python, then in a terminal run `pip install arize-phoenix`.
Start the dashboard with phoenix serve and open it in your browser.
Add Phoenix tracing to your AI app's code, following the docs.

comet-ml/opik.what: Debug, evaluate, and monitor LLM applications, RAG systems, and agentic workflows with comprehensive tracing and automated evaluations.
comet-ml/opik.why: The project solves the need to track, evaluate, and optimize complex multi-step AI agent interactions and LLM calls in production without relying on closed-source SaaS platforms.
comet-ml/opik.caution: Self-hosting the full server platform requires managing backend infrastructure alongside the client SDK.
comet-ml/opik.plain: An open-source dashboard for tracking, testing and grading what your AI app or agent does.
useFor: Record every step an AI agent takes in production
Run automatic quality checks on chatbot answers
Compare prompt versions and keep the best one
steps: Install Python, then in a terminal run `pip install opik`.
Connect it to the hosted Opik service or your own self-hosted server.
Add Opik tracking to your AI app's code, following the docs.

confident-ai/deepeval.what: DeepEval is an open-source evaluation framework for unit testing large language model systems, similar to Pytest.
confident-ai/deepeval.why: It solves the problem of testing and measuring the quality of RAG pipelines, agents, and chatbots, helping you catch regressions and compare prompts or models. Reach for it when you need a rigorous testing harness for your LLM application.
confident-ai/deepeval.plain: A free testing kit that checks whether your AI app's answers are correct, like school exams for chatbots.
useFor: Write pass or fail tests for chatbot answers
Check a document Q&A bot for made-up facts
Run AI quality checks before every release
steps: Install Python, then in a terminal run `pip install deepeval`.
Write a small test file describing inputs and expected answers.
Run the tests with deepeval test run followed by your file name.

Comfy-Org/ComfyUI.what: A modular node graph engine and interface for running and chaining local diffusion models to create images, videos, 3D assets, and audio.
Comfy-Org/ComfyUI.why: It solves the problem of rigid interfaces by allowing complete control over every parameter and model step in local AI generation pipelines. Reach for it when you need a powerful backend or visual workflow builder for complex local diffusion tasks.
Comfy-Org/ComfyUI.start: Download and run the official ComfyUI desktop application or follow the manual installation instructions for your operating system and GPU type.
Comfy-Org/ComfyUI.caution: Complex graph configurations and community custom nodes can sometimes break or cause compatibility issues during weekly updates.
Comfy-Org/ComfyUI.plain: A free app for making AI images, video and audio on your own computer by linking blocks together.
useFor: Generate product images from a text description
Turn a still picture into a short video clip
Reuse a saved workflow to make many similar images
steps: Download the ComfyUI desktop app from the official ComfyUI website.
Open it and let it download a starter image model.
Load a ready-made template workflow, type your description, and press run.
Add community custom nodes carefully, since updates can break them.

AUTOMATIC1111/stable-diffusion-webui.what: A browser-based user interface for running Stable Diffusion image generation models locally.
AUTOMATIC1111/stable-diffusion-webui.why: To generate and edit images, upscale photos, and train custom visual styles using local hardware rather than paid cloud services. Reach for it when you want full control over your image generation pipeline.
AUTOMATIC1111/stable-diffusion-webui.caution: Requires a dedicated GPU with sufficient VRAM (NVIDIA recommended) and significant setup for dependencies.
AUTOMATIC1111/stable-diffusion-webui.plain: A free browser-based app for creating AI images on your own computer with Stable Diffusion.
useFor: Create illustrations from a written description
Fix or replace part of an existing photo
Upscale small images to a larger size
steps: Check that you have a graphics card with enough memory, ideally NVIDIA.
On Windows, download sd.webui.zip from the project's releases page and extract it.
Run update.bat, then run.bat, and open the web page it prints.

lllyasviel/Fooocus.what: Fooocus is an offline image-generating software built on Stable Diffusion XL that focuses on prompting and generation without manual tuning.
lllyasviel/Fooocus.why: It removes the need for complex parameter tweaking and prompt engineering by combining automated prompt processing, inpainting, and image prompts into a simplified offline tool. Reach for it when you want Midjourney-style ease of use locally on your own GPU.
lllyasviel/Fooocus.caution: The project is in a state of limited long-term support (LTS) with bug fixes only and no plans to migrate to newer architectures like Flux.
lllyasviel/Fooocus.plain: A simple free app that makes AI images offline from a short description, with almost no settings.
useFor: Make social media images from a one-line description
Create variations of a picture you already like
Fill in or extend parts of an image
steps: On Windows, download the Fooocus 7z file linked in the README and unzip it.
Double-click run.bat; the first launch downloads the image models automatically.
Type a description in the browser window that opens and press Generate.
Note it only gets bug fixes now, so newer models like Flux are not supported.

openai/whisper.what: Whisper is a general-purpose speech recognition model trained on diverse audio to perform multilingual speech recognition, speech translation, and language identification.
openai/whisper.why: Reach for this when you need to transcribe audio files, translate speech to English, or identify spoken languages locally in your own applications or via the command line.
openai/whisper.caution: Requires external dependencies like ffmpeg and Python packaging tools; the repository has not received updates recently.
openai/whisper.plain: A free AI from OpenAI that turns spoken audio into text in many languages.
useFor: Transcribe a recorded meeting into text
Translate a foreign-language interview into English text
Make subtitles for a video
steps: Prefer an alternative: faster-whisper is quicker and more actively updated.
Install Python and ffmpeg on your computer.
In a terminal, run `pip install -U openai-whisper`.
Transcribe a file by running whisper followed by your audio file name.

SYSTRAN/faster-whisper.what: A reimplementation of OpenAI's Whisper model using CTranslate2 for faster speech recognition and lower memory usage.
SYSTRAN/faster-whisper.why: It speeds up transcription significantly and reduces VRAM/RAM consumption compared to the official Whisper implementation, making it ideal for processing audio files quickly.
SYSTRAN/faster-whisper.caution: Requires specific matching versions of CUDA and cuDNN libraries for GPU acceleration.
SYSTRAN/faster-whisper.plain: A faster, lighter version of OpenAI's Whisper that turns speech recordings into text on your computer.
useFor: Transcribe hours of recordings quickly on your own machine
Add speech-to-text to your own app
Create timestamped subtitles for videos
steps: Install Python on your computer.
In a terminal, run `pip install faster-whisper`.
Write a short Python script that loads a model and transcribes your audio file.
For GPU speed, install the matching CUDA and cuDNN versions listed in the README.

resemble-ai/chatterbox.what: Chatterbox is a family of state-of-the-art text-to-speech models by Resemble AI supporting multilingual generation, voice cloning, and paralinguistic tags.
resemble-ai/chatterbox.why: It provides open-source, high-fidelity voice generation and zero-shot voice cloning models ranging from large multilingual checkpoints down to tiny 110M CPU-friendly models, which you should reach for when building local voice agents or localization workflows.
resemble-ai/chatterbox.plain: Free AI voice models that read text aloud in many languages and can copy a sample voice.
useFor: Turn a written script into a natural voiceover
Clone your own voice from a short recording
Add spoken audio to an app or game
steps: Install Python on your computer.
In a terminal, run `pip install chatterbox-tts`.
Copy the README's short Python example and change the text to yours.
Only clone voices of people who have agreed to it.

hacksider/Deep-Live-Cam.what: Real-time face swap and video deepfake tool powered by a single image.
hacksider/Deep-Live-Cam.why: It lets users perform live face replacement for webcams or video files using just one source image, useful for content creation and character animation. Reach for it when you want real-time face swapping capabilities.
hacksider/Deep-Live-Cam.caution: Requires technical skills for manual installation, or downloading pre-built packages. The project includes content checks for inappropriate media, and users are expected to comply with legal and ethical standards regarding consent and deepfakes.
hacksider/Deep-Live-Cam.plain: An app that swaps your face with another face in live video, using just one photo.
useFor: Try a face swap on a webcam stream
Replace a face in a recorded video clip
Create consented effects for film or comedy sketches
steps: Only use faces of people who have clearly agreed, and follow local deepfake laws.
Download the pre-built quickstart version linked at the top of the README.
Or install it manually with Python and ffmpeg, which the README says needs technical skill.

invoke-ai/InvokeAI.what: Invoke is a creative engine for Stable Diffusion and Flux models featuring a web-based UI, unified canvas, and node-based workflows for generating visual media.
invoke-ai/InvokeAI.why: It provides a robust canvas environment for artists and professionals to generate, inpaint, outpaint, and build customized visual workflows locally.
invoke-ai/InvokeAI.plain: A free creative app for making and editing AI images on your own computer with a drawing canvas.
useFor: Design concept art from a text description
Paint over part of an image and regenerate it
Build repeatable image workflows for a project
steps: Download the Invoke Launcher from the project's launcher releases page.
Run the launcher and let it install Invoke.
Pick a starter model inside the app, then type a description to generate.

coqui-ai/TTS.what: A deep learning toolkit for text-to-speech generation, voice cloning, and training custom voice models.
coqui-ai/TTS.why: It provides pretrained models and training infrastructure to synthesize natural speech or clone voices. Reach for it when you need to add voice generation capabilities to an application or train custom TTS models.
coqui-ai/TTS.caution: The repository was last pushed to in August 2024, so maintenance status should be verified.
coqui-ai/TTS.plain: A free toolkit that turns text into spoken audio and can learn new voices.
useFor: Turn written articles into audio files
Clone a voice from sample recordings
Train a custom voice for a project
steps: Prefer an alternative: Chatterbox is newer and still updated; this repository has not changed since 2024.
Install Python, then in a terminal run `pip install TTS`.
Follow the README examples to pick a model and generate speech.

KKKKhazix/AIHOT.what: A self-hosted web framework that automatically aggregates sources, uses LLMs to filter, score, and cluster news, and generates daily industry briefings.
KKKKhazix/AIHOT.why: Helps you spin up a dedicated industry news aggregator and briefing site customized for any niche field using your own sources and filtering criteria.
KKKKhazix/AIHOT.start:
git clone https://github.com/KKKKhazix/AIHOT.git myhot
cd myhot
node scripts/init-env.ts --llm-key <你的模型 API Key>
docker compose up -d --build
KKKKhazix/AIHOT.caution: The documentation is primarily in Chinese, and setup requires an OpenAI-compatible LLM API key and Docker.
KKKKhazix/AIHOT.plain: A self-hosted website that collects AI news, lets AI pick the important stories, and writes daily briefings.
useFor: Get a daily summary of AI industry news
Track chosen news sources in one place
Build an internal news briefing page for your team
steps: Install Docker and get an API key for an OpenAI-compatible AI model.
In a terminal, clone the repository and set your key with its init-env script, as the README shows.
Start it with `docker compose up -d --build`.
Open http://localhost:3000 in your browser; the docs are mostly in Chinese.

Vincentwei1021/anything2explainer.what: Turns any topic into a motion-graphics explainer video with text-to-speech voiceover and subtitles using Remotion and Claude Code or Codex.
Vincentwei1021/anything2explainer.why: Automates the multi-agent creation of professional programmatic explainer videos from a single prompt. Reach for it when you need to generate educational or technical videos with code-drawn graphics instead of stock footage.
Vincentwei1021/anything2explainer.caution: The repository has no explicit license specified. Requires external dependencies like ffmpeg, espeak-ng, and Python virtual environments, and takes 1 to 3 hours of wall clock time to fully render videos.
Vincentwei1021/anything2explainer.plain: An add-on for Claude Code that turns any topic into an animated explainer video with voice and subtitles.
useFor: Make a short explainer video about a product feature
Turn a lesson topic into a narrated animation
Create subtitled videos for social media
steps: Install Node.js 18 or newer, ffmpeg and Python.
In a terminal, clone the repository and link it into your Claude Code skills folder, as the README shows.
Install the Python voice packages listed in the README.
Inside Claude Code, ask: Make me an explainer video about your topic; rendering can take hours.

yetone/magpie.what: Manage AI models and configure multiple coding agents from a single menu bar interface and local gateway.
yetone/magpie.why: To easily switch models across different AI coding agents and share vendor credentials or local subscriptions without pasting separate keys into every tool.
yetone/magpie.caution: The project was last pushed in September 2026, which may indicate it is unmaintained.
yetone/magpie.plain: A menu bar app that manages your AI models and settings for several coding assistants in one place.
useFor: Switch coding assistants to a different AI model quickly
Keep API keys and model settings in one place
Route several coding tools through one local gateway
steps: Download the app for macOS, Windows or Linux from the Magpie website.
Or install it in a terminal with `curl -fsSL https://usemagpie.ai/install.sh | sh`.
Open Magpie from the menu bar and add your AI models and coding tools.

tigerless-labs/agent-memory.what: Long-term memory runtime for AI agents that uses plain Markdown files as the source of truth, local ranked retrieval, and a sleep-time manage layer.
tigerless-labs/agent-memory.why: AI agents forget everything from past sessions when they close, and agent-memory solves this by providing a local, cross-agent memory store that requires no API keys.
tigerless-labs/agent-memory.caution: Requires Python 3.12 or higher and uv, and is not currently published on PyPI.
tigerless-labs/agent-memory.plain: Gives AI assistants a long-term memory stored as simple text notes on your own computer.
useFor: Let a coding assistant remember past project decisions
Keep AI memories as readable notes you can edit
Share one memory store across several AI tools
steps: Install Python 3.12 or newer and the uv tool.
In a terminal, clone the repository, open its folder and run `uv sync --all-packages`.
Create your memory store by running mem init, then connect it to your agent as the README shows.

dzhng/jevgrep.what: Finds code by asking what it does, helping coding agents discover relevant files and source context.
dzhng/jevgrep.why: Reduces coding agent context discovery costs and token usage when exploring unfamiliar repositories.
dzhng/jevgrep.caution: Searches send eligible source content to third-party AI gateway providers, so avoid pointing it at codebases with sensitive unredacted data if those privacy terms are unsuitable.
dzhng/jevgrep.plain: Helps coding assistants find the right code by describing what it does instead of its exact name.
useFor: Find where login is handled in a large codebase
Help Claude Code locate relevant files faster
Search code by describing its behavior in plain words
steps: Install Node.js, then in a terminal run `npm install -g @dzhng/jevgrep`.
In your project folder, run jg skill so your coding assistant learns to use it.
Avoid sensitive code: searches send code to outside AI services.

2akouwu/reverify.what: Forces coding and reverse-engineering agents to check every claim against deterministic tools before accepting it as fact.
2akouwu/reverify.why: AI models often hallucinate APIs, struct fields, and function behaviors. Reach for this when you need strict ground-truth verification and context preservation during long coding tasks or binary analysis.
2akouwu/reverify.caution: Requires Python and optionally extra native packages like capstone or angr for full functionality.
2akouwu/reverify.plain: Makes AI coding assistants double-check their claims about software files using reliable tools before trusting them.
useFor: Check an AI's analysis of an unknown program file
Stop an assistant from inventing facts about a binary
Give a coding assistant fact-checking tools through MCP
steps: Install Python on your computer.
In a terminal, run `pip install reverify`.
Analyze a file with reverify auto followed by the file name, or connect its MCP server to your assistant.

To3akaRin/mac-computer-use.what: Mac-computer-use is a skill package for AI agents that provides native desktop control, window observation, and accessibility interactions on macOS.
To3akaRin/mac-computer-use.why: Connects AI agents directly to your Mac desktop for tasks requiring window observation, native input, and application automation.
To3akaRin/mac-computer-use.caution: Requires macOS 14+, Swift 6 Command Line Tools, Node.js 22.4+, and explicit Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions on your Mac.
To3akaRin/mac-computer-use.plain: An add-on that lets AI assistants see and click around apps on your Mac.
useFor: Have an AI assistant fill in forms in Mac apps
Let an agent read what is shown in a window
Automate repetitive clicks across desktop apps
steps: Check you have macOS 14 or newer, Node.js 22.4 or newer and Swift command line tools.
In a terminal, run `npx skills add To3akaRin/mac-computer-use`.
Grant Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions in Mac System Settings when asked.

mikehasa/golive-skill.what: An open-source agent skill and Node CLI that helps coding agents take apps live across hosting, databases, domains, email, and payments.
mikehasa/golive-skill.why: It bridges the gap between local app development and production deployment by letting agents detect needs, plan changes, apply them with human approval, and verify the setup without needing a proprietary backend.
mikehasa/golive-skill.caution: Early alpha software with limited live validations; uses plaintext storage for credentials at mode 0600.
mikehasa/golive-skill.plain: An add-on that helps AI coding assistants put your app online, including hosting, domains, email and payments.
useFor: Publish a finished web app to a hosting service
Connect a custom domain and email sending
Get a checklist of what your app needs to launch
steps: In a terminal, run `npx skills add https://github.com/mikehasa/golive-skill --skill golive --global`.
Inside your coding assistant, ask it to take your app live.
Review and approve each planned change; it is early alpha software.

qiz029/dscode.what: A terminal coding agent for macOS built on the DeepSeek Harness featuring persistent shell execution, sub-agent delegation, and cross-session communication.
qiz029/dscode.why: It solves the isolated nature of standard coding agents by allowing multiple local sessions to communicate, share memory, and review each other's work.
qiz029/dscode.caution: Requires macOS 14+ and Node.js 22.19+ or 24+. It integrates with external provider accounts and models.
qiz029/dscode.plain: A coding assistant for the Mac terminal that uses DeepSeek AI models to write and fix code.
useFor: Ask an AI to fix bugs in your project
Let an assistant run commands and tests for you
Use cheaper DeepSeek models for everyday coding
steps: Check you have macOS 14 or newer, Node.js 22.19 or newer, Git and Google Chrome.
In a terminal, run `npm i -g @toddzheng024/dscode`.
Open your project folder in the terminal and type dscode to start.

eternityspring/reelbench-skills.what: A collection of Claude Code and Codex skills for video shot analysis, metadata scrubbing, and storyboard synchronization.
eternityspring/reelbench-skills.why: To perform precise video shot breakdowns, clean metadata tracks, and generate synchronized storyboard reports directly inside your coding agent session. Reach for this when doing AI video workflows that require programmatic inspection or reporting.
eternityspring/reelbench-skills.caution: Requires local FFmpeg and Node.js installation. Relies on the host CLI agent for model execution.
eternityspring/reelbench-skills.plain: Add-ons for Claude Code and Codex that break videos into shots and help plan storyboards.
useFor: Split a video into a shot-by-shot breakdown
Remove hidden metadata from video files
Keep a storyboard in sync with the edited video
steps: Install Node.js 18 or newer and ffmpeg.
In a terminal, clone the repository, open its folder and run `./scripts/install.sh`.
Inside Claude Code or Codex, ask it to analyze a video; the docs are mostly in Chinese.

Jakeschincariol/linkedin-agent-skill.what: Eleven free Claude skills that manage a LinkedIn account by writing posts, comments, replies, and optimizing profiles while removing AI fingerprints.
Jakeschincariol/linkedin-agent-skill.why: Generates professional LinkedIn content and cleans up AI-generated text styles without automating direct posting or risking account bans.
Jakeschincariol/linkedin-agent-skill.caution: Requires manual copy-pasting of generated content because automated posting violates LinkedIn's User Agreement.
Jakeschincariol/linkedin-agent-skill.plain: Free Claude add-ons that write LinkedIn posts, comments and profile text that sound less like AI.
useFor: Draft a LinkedIn post about a recent project
Write thoughtful replies to comments on your posts
Improve your LinkedIn headline and About section
steps: Paste the repository link into Claude Code and ask it to install the skill and confirm /li-post works.
Type /li-post inside Claude Code and describe what you want to share.
Copy the result into LinkedIn yourself; automated posting breaks LinkedIn's rules.

undefined-ui/second-brain-os.what: An AI-powered personal knowledge base that organizes itself inside plain markdown files and Obsidian using Claude Code.
undefined-ui/second-brain-os.why: Solves the problem of accumulating unorganized bookmarks and notes by handing off filing and linking to an automated agent.
undefined-ui/second-brain-os.caution: Requires external setup of Obsidian and Claude Code. The repository contains extensive guides and templates rather than a standalone packaged application.
undefined-ui/second-brain-os.plain: A ready-made notes system for Obsidian that Claude Code keeps organized for you.
useFor: Turn scattered notes into an organized personal knowledge base
Ask Claude questions about your saved notes
Capture ideas daily and let AI file them
steps: Install Obsidian and Claude Code first.
In a terminal, run `git clone https://github.com/undefined-ui/second-brain-os.git`.
Copy the vault template, skills and commands into a new folder, as the README Quickstart shows.
Open that folder in Obsidian and start Claude Code inside it.

okf-memory/okf-agent-memory.what: Provides a git-native persistent memory system for AI coding agents based on the Google Open Knowledge Format (OKF) v0.2, featuring sub-300 microsecond in-memory BM25 search and an embedded Model Context Protocol (MCP) server.
okf-memory/okf-agent-memory.why: Solves context bloat and memory rot in coding agents by separating a compact normative working memory from a semantic pull domain memory. Reach for this when you want persistent, zero-database agent memory that operates entirely via version-controlled plain text.
okf-memory/okf-agent-memory.caution: Requires compiling a Go binary and manually structuring knowledge bundles according to the OKF v0.2 specification.
okf-memory/okf-agent-memory.plain: Gives AI coding assistants a searchable memory saved as files in your project history.
useFor: Let a coding assistant remember project rules between sessions
Search saved project knowledge in a fraction of a second
Share assistant memory with teammates through Git
steps: Install Go and make on your computer.
In a terminal, clone the repository, open its folder and run `make build`.
Organize your notes in the required format, then connect the built-in MCP server to your assistant.

dmoshehun-prog/learn-from-materials.what: Turn books, PDFs, slides, and web pages into traceable knowledge bases and interactive learning web pages.
dmoshehun-prog/learn-from-materials.why: It solves the problem of digesting complex, long-form reading material by automatically extracting structured methodologies, quizzes, and relationship maps for coding agents to process.
dmoshehun-prog/learn-from-materials.caution: Requires an external agent environment like Claude Code, Codex, or WorkBuddy with file system and Python execution access to function.
dmoshehun-prog/learn-from-materials.plain: An add-on that turns your books, PDFs and slides into interactive study web pages with sources.
useFor: Turn a textbook PDF into an interactive study page
Build a knowledge base from lecture slides
Check which page each learned fact came from
steps: Have Claude Code, Codex or a similar assistant installed, plus Python.
In a terminal, run `git clone https://github.com/dmoshehun-prog/learn-from-materials.git ~/.claude/skills/learn-from-materials`.
Inside Claude Code, give it your files and ask for a learning page.

mizzlelover/gongwen-gbt9704-skill.what: Generates editable DOCX documents adhering to the GB/T 9704-2012 Chinese official document standard across multiple AI coding tools and platforms.
mizzlelover/gongwen-gbt9704-skill.why: Ensures official and administrative documents comply with strict government standards (margins, typography, headers, and page numbers) rather than relying on generic AI styling. Reach for it when you need to format structured Chinese official documents for delivery via Word or WPS.
mizzlelover/gongwen-gbt9704-skill.start: node scripts/generate_gongwen_docx.mjs --input tests/fixture.md --output /tmp/gongwen.docx --format ordinary --title "公文格式回归测试"
mizzlelover/gongwen-gbt9704-skill.caution: Requires proper system fonts (such as XiaoBiaoSong and FangSong) for exact compliance; missing standard fonts will trigger fallback warnings or require explicit flags.
mizzlelover/gongwen-gbt9704-skill.plain: An add-on that makes AI tools produce Word files in China's official government document format.
useFor: Turn a draft into a properly formatted official notice
Produce editable Word files that follow GB/T 9704
Format many documents consistently for a government office
steps: Install Node.js and the standard Chinese official fonts, such as FangSong and XiaoBiaoSong.
Add the skill to your AI coding tool following the README.
Ask your assistant to format your text as an official document, or run the included script.

ethanplusai/astra-flash-orchestrator.what: A Codex skill that orchestrates tasks by having an Astra model plan and review while delegating heavy implementation and testing work to DeepSeek Flash.
ethanplusai/astra-flash-orchestrator.why: To dramatically lower token usage and API costs during large coding tasks without sacrificing the architectural judgment of a more capable primary model.
ethanplusai/astra-flash-orchestrator.caution: Early release project. Requires manual prerequisite configuration of Codex, Python 3.11+, and an external router for DeepSeek.
ethanplusai/astra-flash-orchestrator.plain: A Codex add-on where a strong AI plans and reviews while a cheaper DeepSeek model does the heavy work.
useFor: Cut costs on large coding tasks
Have one model plan while another writes code
Get reviewed code changes from a cheaper model
steps: Install Codex and Python 3.11 or newer, and set up a DeepSeek router.
In a terminal, clone the repository and open its folder.
Preview the install with `python3 -B install.py`, then repeat with --apply to install.

alexgreensh/anidoodle.what: Generates hand-drawn art, animations, interactive web graphics, and scored launch films entirely through code.
alexgreensh/anidoodle.why: Used to produce deterministic, code-based illustrations and motion graphics in 31 different artistic styles inside coding agents.
alexgreensh/anidoodle.caution: Requires Claude Code, Codex, or another compatible agent harness to function.
alexgreensh/anidoodle.plain: An add-on for AI coding assistants that creates hand-drawn style art, animations and short films using code.
useFor: Make a hand-drawn illustration for a web page
Create an animated launch video for a product
Draw a chalkboard-style explainer of a concept
steps: Install Claude Code, Codex or Grok Build first.
Inside Claude Code, run `/plugin marketplace add alexgreensh/anidoodle`, then install anidoodle from it.
Describe what you want in plain words, like a risograph lighthouse picture.

LockedinLabs-AI/agent-console.what: Local-first observability tool for tracking token usage, cache performance, and estimated costs of Claude Code and Codex sessions.
LockedinLabs-AI/agent-console.why: Helps developers and teams monitor AI coding agent expenses and session activity locally or across a self-hosted team hub. Reach for it when you want to audit token consumption and cost burn rates without sending your code or prompts to a third-party service.
LockedinLabs-AI/agent-console.start:
git clone https://github.com/LockedinLabs-AI/agent-console.git
cd agent-console
node bin/agent-console.mjs --open
LockedinLabs-AI/agent-console.caution: Requires Node.js 22 or newer. Windows executables are not code-signed.
LockedinLabs-AI/agent-console.plain: A local dashboard that shows how many tokens and how much money your Claude Code and Codex sessions use.
useFor: See which coding sessions cost the most
Track token use over days and weeks
Check how well prompt caching is working
steps: Install Node.js 22 or newer.
In a terminal, clone the repository and open the agent-console folder.
Run `node bin/agent-console.mjs --open` to open the dashboard in your browser.

kaankiziltug/logo-design-skill.what: A comprehensive logo-design skill for Claude and other AI agents that manages discovery, SVG crafting, testing, and client presentation boards.
kaankiziltug/logo-design-skill.why: It brings structured, disciplined brand design workflows directly to AI coding assistants when creating or iterating on brand assets.
kaankiziltug/logo-design-skill.caution: Complex multi-step workflow that relies heavily on agent adherence to structural instructions.
kaankiziltug/logo-design-skill.plain: An add-on that guides Claude through designing a logo, from questions to finished files and a presentation board.
useFor: Design logo ideas for a small business
Get a color palette and icon set for a brand
Create a presentation board to show logo options
steps: For Claude.ai, download logo-design.zip from the Releases page and upload it under Settings, Capabilities, Skills.
For Claude Code, run `/plugin marketplace add kaankiziltug/logo-design-skill` inside Claude Code, then install logo-design.
Describe your business and ask Claude for logo concepts.

jianruntech/geo-score.what: It provides an open rubric and CLI tool to audit websites for AI engine visibility and track citations via LLM APIs.
jianruntech/geo-score.why: It helps developers and site owners understand how well generative search engines like ChatGPT and Perplexity can crawl, understand, and cite their content.
jianruntech/geo-score.caution: Using API features requires providing your own paid provider keys, which will incur API usage costs.
jianruntech/geo-score.plain: A free checker that scores how easily AI search tools like ChatGPT can find and quote your website.
useFor: Check if AI search engines can read your website
Get a fix list to improve AI search visibility
Track whether AI answers cite your site
steps: Install Python on your computer.
In a terminal, run `curl -sL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jianruntech/geo-score/v1.4.0/cli/geo_score.py | python3 - stripe.com --brief` with your site.
Citation tracking needs your own paid AI provider keys.

viettranx/3dviz-pro-max.what: An agent skill for Claude Code and Codex that turns ideas into interactive Three.js and Blender 3D scenes using built-in recipes and knowledge records.
viettranx/3dviz-pro-max.why: Helps coding agents generate visual 3D scenes, animations, and diagrams without requiring manual renderer setup.
viettranx/3dviz-pro-max.caution: Project is maintained as an agent skill; verify output compatibility with your target environment.
viettranx/3dviz-pro-max.plain: An add-on that helps Claude Code and Codex build interactive 3D scenes you can view in a browser.
useFor: Build an interactive 3D product viewer for a web page
Turn an idea into an animated 3D scene
Visualize a concept as a 3D model you can rotate
steps: In a terminal, run `git clone https://github.com/viettranx/3dviz-pro-max.git`.
Copy the whole skills/3dviz-pro-max folder into your Claude Code skills folder, not just SKILL.md.
Start a new Claude Code session and ask for a 3D scene by name.

op7418/guizang-product-video-skill.what: An agent skill that uses code, real product components, and design systems to create software release and update videos with scripts, music, sound effects, and rendering.
op7418/guizang-product-video-skill.why: It bridges the gap between raw codebase updates and polished promotional videos by automating storyboarding, component mounting, and animation using Claude Code or Codex.
op7418/guizang-product-video-skill.caution: This repository has an AGPL-3.0 license and some fallback assets use a Business Source License 1.1. Review all asset and component licensing before commercial distribution.
op7418/guizang-product-video-skill.plain: An add-on that helps AI assistants make release and update videos for software, with script, music and sound.
useFor: Make a short launch video for an app update
Turn release notes into a narrated product video
Create on-brand promo clips from your real interface
steps: In a terminal, run `npx skills add https://github.com/op7418/guizang-product-video-skill --skill guizang-product-video-skill`.
Inside your AI assistant, ask for a product video about your latest release.

Launch cmux and run your preferred CLI coding agents inside it.
Respond to visual blue ring alerts when an agent requires your attention.

openqodex/openqodex.what: OpenQodex is an open-source tool that adds local security scanners and an AI review step to Claude Code or Codex to inspect code changes before they are pushed.

Start the local prediction server with the gutsy-inference command.

nano-muse/nanoMuse.what: An open-source personal AI assistant that runs across your phone, computer, and browser, controlling screens and running commands to automate tasks.
